item.title: 48-hour detention: the plan against troublemakers
item.description: After the events in Bern in 2023, the National Team approved the increase in pretrial detention to 48 hours and greater powers for the sic.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - Parliament discusses tougher measures against violent protesters following the events in Bern in October 2023 - Pre-trial detention from 24 to 48 hours: FDP motions approved in the National Council, awaiting the Council of States - FSA will be able to wiretap phones and plant bugs with court authorization - Organizers of demonstrations will have to pay for security and intervention costs
## Key facts Event: Unauthorized pro-Palestine demonstration that turned violent When: October 2023 Where: Bern Injuries: 18 police officers Key measures: 48-hour detention, FSA powers, costs borne by organizers Legislative status: National Council approved, Council of States to decide in the autumn session Supporting parties: SVP, FDP, The Centre Opposing parties: SP, Young Socialists
### The spark: Bern, October 2023 Almost a year ago, an unauthorized pro-Palestine demonstration turned violent in the center of Bern. Thousands of participants smashed windows, spray-painted walls, and set fire to the tables of the Della Casa restaurant. The police intervention using a water cannon to extinguish the fire got out of hand: 18 officers were injured. The incident triggered a cross-party political reaction that is now reaching Parliament.
### The press conference in the burned-down venue Three weeks after the events, the Swiss Security Alliance held a press conference right in the Della Casa restaurant, still marked by the fire. Representatives from the SVP, FDP, and The Centre attended, presenting a package of measures to contain violent extremism and strengthen internal security. Several parliamentary interventions born from that initiative are now reaching maturity.
### What Parliament has already approved Meanwhile, the Federal Assemblies have approved several motions calling for tougher measures against violent extremism. Many of these will reach the Council of States in the coming days and are expected to be formally adopted in the autumn session. The Social Democratic Party and the Young Socialists condemned the violence during the demonstration but rejected most of the requests, for example on grounds of proportionality.
Discover how the federal legislative process works ### Pre-trial detention doubled: 48 hours instead of 24 The Parliament wants to double the maximum duration of pre-trial detention from 24 to 48 hours. It clearly approved the two PLR motions by Councillor of States Petra Gössi and National Councillor Christian Wasserfallen. However, the two interventions still need to pass in the States. The new regulation should give the police enough time, for example, to secure and evaluate digital traces. And prevent perpetrators of violence after weekend riots from being able to return to work or university on Monday. Moreover, it should grant more time for action to the investigating authorities.
### Strengthened powers for the SIC Already in spring, the Parliament had spoken in favor of granting more powers to the Federal Intelligence Service (SIC). For example, it should be able to gather information covertly before demonstrations where violent extremism is feared. If the court authorizes it, it will be able, for example, to install bugs in private premises and intercept telephone conversations. The request was inserted into the revised Intelligence Service Act, approved by the National Council in June. The decision of the States is expected in the autumn session.
### Organizers called to pay National Councillor Sidney Kamerzin and Councillor of States Charles Juillard (both from The Centre) ask in their motions for a national regulation on the costs of a demonstration. Specifically, organizers should bear, in whole or in part, the costs for security and intervention. In spring, they found a majority in their respective chambers. The next to decide will be the National Council.
### The federalism knot: resistance in Bern and at the federal level Also in the city of Bern, directly affected, several requests have been made after the violent demonstration. Unlike at the federal level, these have a hard time in the Grand Council. As the Berner Zeitung reports, requests such as more funds for the police or a solidarity fund for merchants did not find a majority. Only the intervention to 'verify preventive security measures to protect merchants in case of demonstrations with high risk potential' was transmitted.
The Federal Council rejects the interventions for reasons of federalism. And recently, the Security Commission of the National Council also expressed itself in a contrary manner. The motion interferes with cantonal sovereignty in police matters and violates the principle of subsidiarity. The cantons and municipalities have already issued regulations in this regard, so there is no need for intervention at the federal level. This clash between the federal level and cantonal autonomy is the heart of the debate: how much can Bern legislate on security and public order without invading cantonal competencies?
### Practical implications for those who demonstrate and for those who organize If the measures also pass in the States, those who participate in demonstrations that degenerate into violence risk staying in jail 48 hours instead of 24, with consequences on work, study, and private life. Organizers will have to budget potentially high costs for security and police intervention, which could discourage the organization of marches on sensitive topics. Preventive SIC surveillance raises questions about privacy and proportionality: who decides when 'violent extremism is feared'? The parliamentary debate reflects a tension between security and civil liberties that touches fundamental rights guaranteed by the Federal Constitution.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### What happens next: timeline and upcoming steps The autumn session of the Federal Assembly is the decisive moment. The Council of States will have to rule on: PLR motions for 48-hour detention (Gössi and Wasserfallen), the revised Intelligence Services Act with expanded SIS powers, and Centre Party motions on costs borne by organizers (Kamerzin and Juillard). The National Council will then have to confirm or reject the decisions of the Council of States. Exact dates for individual votes have not been announced.
### How to follow the legislative process Citizens can consult the Parliament website (parliament.ch) for: full texts of motions and bills, meeting minutes, voting results, and the positions of individual parliamentarians. The relevant committees (Security Committee, Legal Affairs Committee) publish reports explaining the substance of the proposals.
### Rights and duties in demonstrations: what to know The Federal Constitution (Art. 22) guarantees freedom of assembly. Unauthorized demonstrations are not inherently prohibited, but the police can disperse them if they turn violent. Anyone committing acts of violence, damage, or resistance to public officials faces criminal liability. Pre-trial detention (Art. 221 CPP) serves to secure evidence and prevent the repetition of crimes. With the potential extension to 48 hours, the police will have more time for technical investigations (smartphone analysis, facial recognition, movement tracking).
### Useful tools for orientation To understand how legislative changes on security and public order may impact daily rights and duties, it is useful to compare current regulations with the proposals under discussion. Our salary/tax calculator includes modules to simulate the tax impacts of potential criminal fines. [Calculate your net salary and check scenarios](nav:calculator)
Stay informed: the decisions of the autumn session will define the framework for the coming years. Those who organize or participate in demonstrations, those who manage businesses in sensitive areas, and those working in public security: everyone will have to deal with the new rules if they come into effect.

item.title: TranspaReg: Frames request deferral for cyber risk
item.description: National Councillor Lorenzo Quadri asks to suspend the entry into force on 1 October, citing the case of Liechtenstein.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - Quadri chiede di sospendere TranspaReg al 1° ottobre - Rischio informatico per dati di 500'000 entità - Caso Liechtenstein: dati di 31'000 aziende sottratti - Obiettivo GAFI: trasparenza ADE senza centralizzazione
## Fatti chiave - Chi: Consigliere nazionale Lorenzo Quadri (Lega dei Ticinesi) - Quando: Entrata in vigore prevista il 1° ottobre - Cosa: Registro svizzero per la trasparenza degli ADE - Dove: Svizzera (scala nazionale) - Rischio: Attacchi informatici su database centralizzato
Il Consigliere nazionale Lorenzo Quadri, rappresentante della Lega dei Ticinesi, ha presentato una mozione al Consiglio federale con una richiesta precisa: sospendere l’entrata in vigore della TranspaReg, prevista per il prossimo 1° ottobre. L’obiettivo è guadagnare tempo per valutare soluzioni alternative alla centralizzazione dei dati, che Quadri considera troppo rischiosa. Il nuovo registro svizzero per la trasparenza degli aventi economicamente diritto (ADE) ha lo scopo di raccogliere le informazioni sulle persone fisiche che controllano effettivamente società, fondazioni, trust e altre strutture giuridiche. Si tratta di un passo cruciale per la conformità alle norme internazionali, ma il consigliere mette in guardia contro i pericoli di un database unico.
### Il timore della centralizzazione
Secondo Quadri, la concentrazione in un unico sistema di dati sensibili relativi a oltre 500'000 società ed entità rappresenta un rischio considerevole per la sicurezza nazionale. Il timore principale riguarda la vulnerabilità informatica: una banca dati di queste dimensioni costituirebbe un bersaglio particolarmente appetibile per la criminalità informatica. Il consigliere cita l’evoluzione dell’intelligenza artificiale, che permetterebbe agli attaccanti di sviluppare strategie sempre più sofisticate per violare i sistemi di protezione. La mozione sottolinea che la reputazione finanziaria svizzera sarebbe a forte rischio in caso di violazione. Quadri invita il Governo a verificare se gli obiettivi di trasparenza richiesti dal GAFI possano essere raggiunti attraverso sistemi più sicuri, ad esempio decentralizzati, evitando così di esporre l’intero paese a un singolo punto di fallimento.
Per chi vive e lavora in Svizzera, la stabilità del quadro giuridico e la protezione dei dati aziendali sono fattori determinanti per l’attività economica. La richiesta di rinvio non è un ostacolo alla trasparenza, ma un invito a costruire un sistema robusto. La decisione spetterà ora al Consiglio federale, che dovrà bilanciare le pressioni internazionali con la necessità di garantire la sicurezza informatica del paese. I cittadini e le imprese possono seguire l’evoluzione della mozione attraverso i canali parlamentari ufficiali. La questione tocca da vicino le 500'000 entità coinvolte, ognuna delle quali dovrà comunque garantire la tracciabilità dei propri ADE, indipendentemente dalla modalità di archiviazione scelta dallo Stato. La prudenza in questo campo non è solo tecnica, ma economica e reputazionale. L’analisi delle implicazioni pratiche della mozione di Quadri rivela un conflitto tra obblighi internazionali e sicurezza informatica. Il registro TranspaReg mira a soddisfare i requisiti del GAFI (Gruppo di Azione Finanziaria), che impone la trasparenza degli aventi economicamente diritto per lotta al riciclaggio e al finanziamento del terrorismo. Tuttavia, la modalità di implementazione, se centralizzata, crea un rischio sistematico. Il caso del Liechtenstein, citato nella mozione, è un precedente allarmante: a fine luglio, il registro analogo del Principato è stato colpito da un attacco informatico con la sottrazione di dati relativi agli ADE di circa 31'000 aziende, fondazioni e trust. Questo incidente dimostra che il rischio non è teorico, ma concreto e attuale.
### Confronto scenari: centralizzato vs decentralizzato
Un sistema centralizzato offre un accesso unificato e semplificato per le autorità, ma concentra il rischio. Un sistema decentralizzato, invece, frammenta i dati, rendendo più difficile un attacco massiccio. Quadri sostiene che gli obiettivi di trasparenza possono essere raggiunti anche con architetture distribuite, che offrono maggiore resilienza. Per le imprese svizzere, questo significa che la procedura di dichiarazione degli ADE potrebbe mantenere i medesimi requisiti di contenuto, ma cambiare la piattaforma di invio. È fondamentale che le aziende si preparino a possibili cambiamenti di procedura senza ritardi nella conformità. La mozione ricorda inoltre una presa di posizione degli operatori del settore, che avrebbero espresso preoccupazione al DFGP (Dipartimento federale della gestione pubblica). Questo segnale dall’industria finanziaria è un dato importante: il settore bancario e assicurativo, pilastro dell’economia svizzera, vede nella sicurezza dei dati un elemento critico per la fiducia degli investitori internazionali. Un eventuale rinvio permetterebbe di coinvolgere gli esperti tecnici e giuridici nella progettazione di un sistema a prova di future minacce. La reputazione della piazza finanziaria svizzera, basata sulla stabilità e sulla riservatezza, sarebbe a rischio in caso di violazione, con danni economici difficili da quantificare e da invertire.
### Impatto sulla fiducia degli investitori
La mozione di Quadri non è un’opposizione alla trasparenza, ma una richiesta di prudenza tecnica. La Svizzera deve dimostrare di poter rispettare gli standard internazionali senza compromettere la sicurezza dei propri cittadini e delle proprie imprese. Il dibattito parlamentare che ne seguirà è un’occasione per definire un modello di governance dei dati più robusto. Per i residenti in Svizzera, la stabilità di questo sistema si riflette nella sicurezza delle proprie transazioni e nella protezione della propria identità economica. La scelta tra centralizzazione e decentralizzazione avrà ripercussioni su come le autorità accesseranno i dati in futuro, influenzando l’efficienza dei controlli e la protezione dei diritti degli interessati. La decisione finale dovrà tenere conto dell’evoluzione tecnologica, in particolare dell’impatto dell’intelligenza artificiale sulla sicurezza informatica. Un approccio troppo rigido potrebbe rendere il sistema obsoleto o vulnerabile nel breve termine, mentre un approccio troppo cauto rischierebbe di non soddisfare i requisiti del GAFI. Il Consiglio federale ha ora la responsabilità di trovare un equilibrio che protegga sia la reputazione del paese sia la sicurezza dei dati dei suoi cittadini.

1. Verify your registration: ensure that ADE data is up to date and consistent with current regulations, regardless of the final archiving platform. 2. item.description: The initiative to insert a constitutional mandate on the school will be submitted to the voters on September 27, 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Popular initiative to include a mandate on school quality in the Bernese Constitution - Voting scheduled for 27 September 2026 - Promoted by the Cantonal Teachers' Association, opposed by the government and bourgeois parties
## Key facts - Initiative: Bern quality school - Voting date: 27 September 2026 - Promoters: Cantonal Teachers' Association - Opponents: Cantonal Government, Majority Grand Council, UDC, PLR, Alleanza del Centro, UDF, Cantonal Economic Organizations - Main supporter: Bildung Bern (Director Stefan Widmer)
### The context of the initiative In the Canton of Bern, as in the rest of Switzerland, the school faces a shortage of qualified staff, large classes and an increase in administrative tasks that take time away from teaching. To respond to these difficulties, the Cantonal Teachers' Association has launched a popular initiative calling for the inclusion in the cantonal constitution of an explicit mandate in favour of school quality. According to Stefan Widmer, director of Bildung Bern, the aim of the initiative is to ensure sufficiently qualified staff and relieve them of bureaucratic tasks, so that they can focus more on teaching. The idea is to invest where the effect is greatest to promote the academic success of pupils and students.
Opposition is transversal. The Cantonal Government, the ### Analysis of possible consequences If accepted, the initiative would introduce a constitutional obligation for the Canton of Bern to guarantee adequate resources for the quality of schools. This could translate into greater financial commitment from the canton, even though the source does not specify amounts or percentages. In practice, the mandate could lead to a revision of spending priorities, with a possible increase in funds allocated to teaching staff and a reduction in administrative duties.
On the contrary, if the initiative were rejected, the status quo would be maintained. The cantonal government and opposing political forces argue that current laws are sufficient and that improvements should come through operational measures, such as hiring new teachers or simplifying bureaucratic procedures. In this scenario, schools would continue to rely on existing funding mechanisms, without a constitutional constraint requiring the allocation of specific resources.
Another aspect to consider is the impact on personnel management. The stated objective of the promoters is to have more qualified teachers who are less burdened by bureaucratic tasks. If the mandate were accepted, the canton might be pushed to invest in continuing education and support services that free up time for teaching. This could have positive repercussions on teaching staff motivation and, potentially, on student outcomes.
Finally, the vote on September 27 represents a moment of direct participation by Bernese citizens in educational policy decisions. The result may influence not only the internal debate within the canton but also the comparison at the Swiss level on how to address common challenges of the school system, such as teacher shortages and the increase in administrative workload.

1. Find out the exact text of the popular initiative. The official document is published on the Bern State Chancellery website and contains the proposed constitutional mandate.
2. Follow the communications of the parties involved. On the portal of the cantonal government you can find the communiqués of the Council of State, while the promoting and opposing committees regularly publish updates on their sites and social networks.
3. Check the date of the vote: September 27, 2026. Register with the electoral register if you have not already done so and check your polling place indicated in the letter of call to the polls.
4. If you want to understand how any public spending decisions may affect your personal situation, you can use calculation tools available online. For example, to get an estimate of your net income after taxes, you can use the calculator offered by the site.
5. After collecting the information, go to the polling station on the day of the vote and express your yes or no preference on the initiative.

item.title: Production and import prices: +0.7% in August 2026
item.description: The producer and import price index rises to 100.4 points in August 2026. On an annual basis, there is a decrease of 0.7% according to UST data.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Producer and Import Price Index: +0.7% compared to July 2026 - Index level: 100.4 points (base Dec. 2025 = 100) - Annual decrease: -0.7% compared to August 2025 - Data published on September 14, 2026, by the FSO
## Key facts - Publication date: September 14, 2026 - Monthly variation: 0.7% - Index value: 100.4 - Annual variation: -0.7% - Data source: FSO
Neuchâtel, September 14, 2026. The Federal Statistical Office (FSO) has released updated data on producer and import price trends in Switzerland. The official press release, dated September 14, 2026, reveals that in August 2026, the total producer and import price index recorded an increase of 0.7% compared to the previous month. This increase brings the index level to 100.4 points, using December 2025 as the reference base, set at 100 points.
### Market dynamics The monthly rise was primarily driven by specific industrial and energy sectors. FSO data show a particular increase in the prices of petroleum products, chemical products, as well as those related to crude oil and natural gas. Specifically, the increase in the producer price index compared to the previous month is mainly due to higher prices for petroleum products and pharmaceutical preparations. Price increases were also observed for slaughter pigs, pork, raw milk, rubber and plastic products, as well as plastics in primary forms.
However, the picture is not uniformly positive for costs. The FSO reports a decrease in the prices of basic pharmaceutical products, other chemical products, and electricity for large consumers. On the import side, compared to July 2026, the import price index recorded higher prices especially for petroleum products, organic products of the chemical industry, crude oil, and natural gas. Increases were also recorded for plastics in primary forms, vegetables, melons and potatoes, rubber and plastic products, inorganic products of the chemical industry, other chemical products, paper and paper products, and green coffee. Conversely, a drop in computer prices was observed.
On a trend level, the situation shows stabilization. Compared to August 2025, the price level of the total supply of domestic and imported products fell by 0.7%. This figure indicates that, despite the monthly inflationary push, national price pressure remains below the level recorded a year ago. Full results and further information on the subject can be found on the FSO website, which is the official source for these crucial economic indicators for the Swiss economy. item.title: Naturalization in Nidvaldo: requirements and procedure
item.description: Complete guide to ordinary naturalization in the Canton of Nidvaldo: required years, tests, taxes and bureaucratic steps.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - C permit required - Years of residence required by regulations - Language and integration tests necessary - Cantonal and municipal procedure
## Key facts - Permit: Permit C - Levels involved: Federal, cantonal, and municipal - Requirements: Integration and language - Authority: Competent offices of the Canton of Nidwalden
The path to Swiss citizenship in the Canton of Nidwalden follows a well-defined process that combines federal directives with specific cantonal and municipal provisions. Those who reside in Swiss territory and wish to obtain the red passport must deal with a system structured across multiple institutional levels, where cooperation between the Confederation, the Canton, and the individual municipality of residence represents the cornerstone of the entire procedure. To initiate the ordinary naturalization process, the fundamental preliminary requirement is the possession of a valid C residence permit, a document that certifies the stability of the stay on national territory. The reference legislation establishes precise time parameters regarding the years of residence necessary to be able to submit the official application to the competent offices.
### The basic regulatory framework The Swiss system provides that obtaining citizenship is not an automatic act, but the result of a successful integration path. In the Canton of Nidwalden, the authorities in charge carefully verify compliance with all criteria established by current provisions. The procedure starts at the local level, where the applicant must demonstrate being rooted in the community in which they live. This bond translates into respect for the Swiss legal order, participation in social and economic life, and the ability to provide for one's own livelihood and that of family members without resorting to social assistance, barring rare exceptions provided by law. Each phase of the investigation requires the production of official documentation issued by the competent administrative bodies, which certifies the irreproachable conduct of the applicant and the absence of pending charges or significant criminal proceedings. The practical analysis of the naturalization procedure in the Canton of Nidwalden highlights the importance of thorough preparation by the candidate. In addition to complying with residency time limits, which also take into account the period spent with certain permits according to the provisions of the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM), a decisive weight is played by language and integration checks. The candidate must demonstrate a sufficient knowledge of the national language spoken in the region, proving that they can communicate effectively both in daily life and in work or administrative contexts. The cantonal authorities set up specific checks to ascertain that the foreign citizen knows the institutional, historical and cultural peculiarities of Switzerland and the Canton of Nidwalden.
Integration checks and tests The evaluation path includes targeted exams to test the knowledge of Swiss political institutions, federalism, and civic rights and duties. For those living in Nidwalden, understanding the functioning of direct democracy, including federal voting and ballot mechanisms, constitutes an essential element of the civic suitability exam. Local authorities also evaluate professional and economic integration, verifying the regularity of the tax and contribution position, including regular payments of cantonal, municipal and direct federal taxes, as well as compulsory health care insurance coverage through a recognized health insurance fund under KAMal/LAMal. Any pending debts, enforcement procedures or loss certificates can seriously compromise the positive outcome of the application, making a stable and transparent financial situation essential before sending the dossier.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). The operational phase of the request requires compliance with rigorous procedural steps at the offices of the Canton of Nidwalden and the municipality of residence. Before submitting the official form, it is advisable to gather all necessary documents, including criminal record extracts, updated civil status certificates, residency certificates, and tax documentation issued by the competent authorities. The fees to be paid for processing the procedure vary based on cantonal and municipal tariff provisions and cover the administrative costs required for the review of the dossier by the various entities involved. Once the application has been filed, waiting times may vary depending on the workload of the offices and the complexity of the requirements check.
### Procedure and Next Steps After the preliminary review at the municipal level, the file is forwarded to the cantonal bodies for final approval, which is also subject to the issuance of federal authorization by the competent authorities. Throughout this period, the applicant must continuously maintain residency in the municipality of Nidwalden. item.title: Federal Council decisions: news and votes 2026
item.description: The latest news and projects of the Federal Council: from women in voluntary service to climate protection and popular voting.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Bill for women's voluntary service project - Goal of zero CO2 emissions by the administration by 2040 - Public vote scheduled for September 27, 2026 - Measures for heatwaves, drought, forests, and agriculture
## Key facts - Body: Federal Council - Public vote date: September 27, 2026 - Voting topics: Neutrality initiative and food initiative - EU package transmission date: March 13, 2026
The official website of the Swiss Government provides up-to-date information on the decisions and activities of the Federal Council, its functioning as a collegial body, as well as on popular votes. Among the topics at the center of institutional attention are recent legislative initiatives and major national deadlines that directly involve the administration and citizens residing on Swiss territory. The federal authorities continue to publish details regarding upcoming trips to the polls and projects currently undergoing parliamentary review.
### Legislative projects and reforms Swiss women will be required to participate in an information day on the army and civil protection. The Federal Council has submitted to Parliament a bill aimed at encouraging women to perform voluntary service. Meanwhile, the central federal administration must play an exemplary role in the field of climate protection and must reduce CO2 emissions to zero by 2040. A further development concerns the promotion of fiber optics in sparsely populated areas, for which the executive has approved the message relating to the broadband support law to be submitted to Parliament for discussion and formal approval. The activity of the Federal Council also touches on the management of environmental and climate emergencies on the national territory. In response to seasonal criticalities, the Federal Council has decided to take further measures to cope with periods of heatwave and drought. The additional funds allocated in this context will be earmarked specifically for forests and agriculture, sectors that are particularly vulnerable to prolonged climate change. The evolution of these measures and the general situation will be reassessed at the end of October by the competent authorities.
### International relations and electoral appointments A major chapter concerns diplomatic and economic relations with the European Union. Switzerland and the EU have negotiated a new package of agreements aimed at stabilising and developing bilateral relations. item.title: Petrol today costs less than in the 1980s
item.description: The price of petrol is around CHF 2/litre, lower than the value of the 1980s adjusted for purchasing power (CHF 3.50) and more advantageous than in many foreign countries.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Gasoline in Switzerland is cheaper than in the past when adjusted for purchasing power. - Today's price is lower than in the 1980s, even after accounting for inflation. - The cost of gasoline has a smaller impact on the Swiss budget compared to other countries.
## Key Facts Gas price (approx.): 2 CHF/liter 1980s price comparison (nominal): 1.25 CHF/liter 1980s price (adjusted for inflation): 2.37 CHF/liter 1980s price (adjusted for purchasing power): 3.50 CHF/liter Modern car consumption vs 40-50 years ago: half
The price of gasoline, often a subject of debate and crossing the psychological threshold of two francs per liter, does not represent a significant cost when compared to the past and other countries, especially when considering average purchasing power. Philippe Thalmann, a professor of economics at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne (EPFL), emphasizes that Switzerland ranks among the nations with the most affordable fuel prices relative to average incomes. In most other parts of the world, gasoline expenses weigh much more heavily on household budgets compared to the Swiss Confederation.
### International Comparative Analysis The professor cites Vietnam as an emblematic example: a liter of gasoline costs about half as much as in Switzerland, but in relation to average income, the cost of the same amount of fuel is eight times higher. This would translate for a Swiss consumer to an equivalent cost of approximately 16 francs per liter. Even more extreme situations exist in Ghana, where the equivalent cost would be around 33 francs per liter, and in Nepal, reaching up to 65 francs per liter. These comparisons highlight how the perception of gasoline costs is closely tied to the local economic context and the purchasing power of citizens. The war in Iran has led to an increase in electric car purchases in Vietnam, a trend not yet replicated in Switzerland, suggesting that significantly higher fuel prices could incentivize behavioral changes in the Confederation, pushing toward more efficient or electric vehicles and alternative forms of mobility.
### The Historical Perspective: The 1980s A look at the past reveals that fuels today are less expensive than in the 1980s. Following the second oil crisis, between the late 1970s and early 1980s, the price of oil reached record levels, bringing gasoline to about 1.25 francs per liter. If these prices were adjusted for inflation, a liter of gasoline would cost nearly 2.37 francs today. Even more pronounced is the difference if purchasing power is considered: in that case, the price would rise to approximately 3.50 francs per liter. This demonstrates that, despite current fluctuations, the real cost of fuel has decreased over time, also thanks to significant improvements in the efficiency of combustion engines. Modern cars consume about half the fuel to cover the same distance compared to models from 40 or 50 years ago, even though they have become heavier and more powerful. Consequently, a modern car with a full tank can travel double the distance compared to a decade ago, making gasoline even more economical in terms of kilometers traveled per franc spent. ### L'Impatto dell'Efficienza Energetica e del Potere d'Acquisto L'evoluzione tecnologica ha giocato un ruolo cruciale nel rendere il costo della benzina meno impattante sui bilanci svizzeri. Le automobili di oggi, pur essendo più grandi e potenti rispetto ai modelli di 40-50 anni fa, consumano in media la metà del carburante per percorrere 100 chilometri. Questo incremento di efficienza si traduce in un raddoppio dell'autonomia con un pieno, rispetto a quanto era possibile decenni fa. Pertanto, sebbene il prezzo nominale alla pompa possa sembrare elevato, il costo per chilometro percorso è effettivamente diminuito. Philippe Thalmann evidenzia come, in termini di potere d'acquisto e considerando l'evoluzione dei prezzi, il carburante sia oggi meno costoso rispetto all'inizio degli anni Ottanta. Per comprendere appieno queste dinamiche, è fondamentale distinguere tra prezzi corretti per l'inflazione e prezzi corretti per il potere d'acquisto. I primi neutralizzano l'aumento generale dei prezzi nel tempo, mentre i secondi permettono di valutare quanto un bene incida sul bilancio delle famiglie in periodi diversi o tra Paesi con livelli di reddito differenti.
### Percezione del Costo e Comportamenti dei Consumatori Nonostante i dati economici suggeriscano una convenienza del carburante rispetto al passato e al contesto internazionale, la percezione del prezzo rimane un fattore soggettivo. Se i due franchi al litro vengono percepiti come eccessivi, ci si aspetterebbe una reazione da parte dei consumatori, orientata al risparmio di carburante o alla scelta di alternative. Tuttavia, i dati più recenti dell'Ufficio federale delle strade (USTRA) indicano una tendenza al rialzo del volume del traffico, suggerendo che i comportamenti non siano ancora significativamente cambiati. Anche il mercato della mobilità elettrica in Svizzera non mostra, al momento, un'impennata delle immatricolazioni paragonabile a quella osservata in altri Paesi in risposta all'aumento dei prezzi del petrolio. Questo stallo nei cambiamenti comportamentali potrebbe essere legato a diversi fattori, tra cui la stabilità relativa dei prezzi dei carburanti in Svizzera negli ultimi anni rispetto ad altri mercati, o una minore sensibilità del consumatore svizzero alle fluttuazioni dei prezzi del petrolio, data la maggiore capacità di spesa media. L'economista suggerisce che solo un aumento sostanziale e prolungato dei prezzi potrebbe fungere da reale catalizzatore per un cambiamento nelle abitudini di consumo e nella scelta dei veicoli, orientando così il mercato verso soluzioni più sostenibili e meno dipendenti dai combustibili fossili. La correlazione tra prezzo percepito e azione concreta rimane quindi un punto cruciale per comprendere l'evoluzione futura della mobilità in Svizzera, influenzando potenzialmente anche le politiche fiscali future relative ai carburanti e ai veicoli.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ### Comprendere il Costo Reale del Carburante Per valutare correttamente il costo della benzina in Svizzera, è essenziale considerare non solo il prezzo nominale alla pompa, ma anche fattori come l'inflazione e il potere d'acquisto. Come spiegato dal professore Philippe Thalmann, confrontare il prezzo attuale con quello degli anni '80, tenendo conto dell'inflazione, rivela che il carburante è oggi significativamente meno costoso. Un prezzo di 1,25 franchi al litro negli anni '80 equivalrebbe oggi a circa 2,37 franchi, se corretto per l'inflazione, e a circa 3,50 franchi se aggiustato per il potere d'acquisto. Questo significa che, in proporzione al reddito medio, il costo effettivo del carburante è diminuito nel tempo. Inoltre, l'aumento dell'efficienza dei veicoli ha ulteriormente ridotto il costo per chilometro percorso. Un'automobile moderna consuma circa la metà del carburante rispetto a un modello di 40-50 anni fa per coprire la stessa distanza. Ciò implica che, con un pieno, un'auto attuale può percorrere il doppio dei chilometri rispetto al passato, rendendo di fatto il carburante più economico in termini di mobilità effettiva. Questi dati suggeriscono che la percezione di un prezzo elevato della benzina potrebbe essere più legata a fattori psicologici o a un confronto con altri beni e servizi, piuttosto che a una reale diminuzione del potere d'acquisto rispetto al passato.
### Implicazioni e Scenari Futuri Sebbene i dati mostrino una relativa convenienza del carburante in Svizzera, sia rispetto al passato che ad altri Paesi, l'economista Philippe Thalmann avverte che un aumento significativo dei prezzi potrebbe innescare un cambiamento nelle abitudini dei consumatori. Un costo della benzina comparabile a quello di Paesi come il Vietnam (in proporzione al reddito) o addirittura più elevato, fungerebbe da forte incentivo a ridurre i consumi, ad adottare veicoli elettrici o più efficienti, o a optare per forme di mobilità alternative. Al momento, tuttavia, non si osservano cambiamenti drastici nei comportamenti di mobilità in Svizzera. I dati sull'aumento del traffico e la mancanza di un'impennata nelle immatricolazioni di veicoli elettrici suggeriscono che i prezzi attuali, pur superando la soglia dei due franchi al litro, non sono ancora sufficientemente dissuasivi per alterare significativamente le abitudini consolidate. Le autorità federali e cantonali monitorano costantemente l'evoluzione del mercato e le abitudini dei consumatori, ma per ora non sembrano esserci le condizioni per un ripensamento radicale delle politiche energetiche legate alla mobilità. Il confronto con il passato e con altri Paesi rimane uno strumento utile per contestualizzare il costo attuale del carburante, ma le future dinamiche dipenderanno dall'equilibrio tra prezzo, efficienza tecnologica e sensibilità dei consumatori. In the context of Canton Nidwalden, the issuance of the C settlement permit represents an important milestone for foreign citizens wishing to establish themselves permanently in Swiss territory. For citizens belonging to the European Union and the European Free Trade Association, the ordinary term provided is generally five years of continuous regular residence in the country. For third-country nationals, the general rule instead provides for a period of ten years. However, compliance with these timeframes represents only the first of the necessary requirements. This aspect includes several key factors, among which a stable employment situation and knowledge of the official language spoken in the region stand out. Participation in the country's economic life, through regular work activity or an autonomous source of income, constitutes a further fundamental pillar for the acceptance of the request.

item.title: Agricultural studies: low earnings for milk in Switzerland
item.description: A recent FHNW study reveals that dairy farmers earn on average 8.30 francs per hour, compared to 73.60 francs for rapeseed.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Milk producers earn an average of 8.30 francs per hour. - Rapeseed production yields 73.60 francs per hour, about nine times more. - 35% of Swiss agricultural businesses operate in the dairy sector. - For a fair income, the price of milk should rise by 77%.
## Key facts - Study: Fachhochschule Nordwestschweiz (FHNW) - Client: Faire Märkte Schweiz - Hourly earnings for suckler cows: 4.30 francs - Hourly earnings for beef cattle fattening: 7.90 francs - Hourly earnings for sugar beets: 55.90 francs - Necessary increase for beef: 39% - Necessary increase for suckler cows: 101%
A recent study conducted by the Fachhochschule Nordwestschweiz (FHNW), commissioned by the association Faire Märkte Schweiz, has highlighted significant gaps in the hourly incomes of Swiss farmers. The data, released on September 13, 2026, show how milk production, which accounts for 35% of all agricultural businesses in the country, is in a state of extreme economic difficulty. Suckler cow breeders earn barely 4.30 francs per hour, while those dealing with beef cattle fattening reach 7.90 francs. The average for milk producers stands at 8.30 francs per hour, a figure that appears clearly lower compared to other agricultural sectors.
### The contrast with plant crops Research highlights a clear gap between livestock farming and plant cultivation. While the dairy sector suffers, sugar beet production yields 55.90 francs per hour. Even more advantageous is rapeseed, with an hourly earning of 73.60 francs. The study's author, FHNW economist Mathias Binswanger, clarifies that the differences depend largely on the required labor commitment and the possibility of automation. In plant cultivation, located predominantly in the plains, many steps are automated, reducing operating costs. Conversely, animal farming presents structural constraints that prevent the same production efficiency, making the work more burdensome and less remunerative for those who practice it daily in the field. Income dynamics in the Swiss agricultural sector depend not only on operational efficiency, but also on exogenous variables that hit producers hard. Increasingly frequent extreme weather events directly affect fodder cultivation. This dependency creates a ripple effect that impacts milk and meat production, making it difficult for farmers to react to market price fluctuations. As Binswanger pointed out, the rigidity in the number of farmed animals prevents a rapid adjustment of supply, exposing businesses to constant financial risks that do not affect seasonal crops in the same way.
### Impact on consumer prices To guarantee farmers a wage comparable to other regional incomes, the study suggests the need for a significant increase in production prices. It is estimated that for milk, an increase of 77% would be necessary. Regarding beef, the indicated threshold is 39%, while for suckler cows the increase should reach 101%. It is essential to understand that these percentages refer exclusively to the producer price and do not automatically translate into an identical price hike on store shelves. The final cost paid by consumers depends on the margins applied by processors and retailers that make up the supply chain. This mechanism of transferring the price increase makes the final consumer price a variable and complex data point, influenced by commercial logics that often leave the primary production link in a weak negotiating position. The economic stability of farmers therefore remains closely tied to the ability to negotiate more adequate prices with buyers, especially in view of seasons that, on the climate front, promise to be increasingly hostile. ## Key facts - **What**: FSO cultural economy statistics - When: September 11, 2026 - Where: Neuchâtel, Switzerland - Who: Federal Statistical Office (FSO) - Amount: 69,441 active enterprises
In 2024, with nearly 70,000 active cultural enterprises in Switzerland, a new record was reached: a 27% increase compared to 2011. These are some of the latest findings from the cultural economy statistics compiled by the Federal Statistical Office (FSO).
In 2024, there were 69,441 active enterprises in the cultural sector. This represents a 1.8% increase compared to the previous year and a new record since 2011, the first year the statistics were produced. Compared to 2019, before the COVID-19 pandemic, Switzerland had 7.2% more cultural enterprises and a quarter more than in 2011. Since 2011, the number of enterprises has increased by 15.6% in the general economy, meaning cultural enterprises are becoming increasingly numerous: while they accounted for 9.8% of total enterprises in 2011, the percentage rose to 10.5% in 2019 and 10.7% in 2024.
### Cultural heritage and performing arts
The number of cultural enterprises showed very variable trends depending on the branch of activity. The increase recorded between 2023 and 2024 was evident in the cultural heritage sector (+3.8% of enterprises) and the performing arts (+3.3%), while it was particularly marked in the audiovisual and multimedia creative sectors (+6.5%) and advertising (+6.3%). In the artistic craftsmanship sector, the number of enterprises recorded a slight decrease (-0.6%), whereas the books and printing sector saw a sharp decline (-3.1%). In the latter sector, the number of enterprises in 2024 even dropped by 12.3% compared to 2019, keeping in mind that this figure had already been steadily declining since 2015. Despite the increase in the number of businesses, the number of jobs in the cultural sector decreased in 2024: with 241,025 jobs, a decline compared to the previous year (-0.9%) was recorded for the first time since 2020. Compared to the economy as a whole, where the number of jobs showed a more pronounced increase, a slow contraction of the cultural sector's share has been observed since 2011: in 2011, the cultural sector still accounted for 4.7% of total employment, by 2019 the percentage had dropped to 4.4%, and in 2024, despite the growing number of cultural enterprises, to 4.2%.
Cultural enterprises, which are growing in number, are therefore becoming increasingly smaller. While in 2011 a cultural enterprise had an average of 4.1 jobs, by 2024 the number had dropped to 3.5. Over the same period, full-time equivalents (FTEs) per cultural enterprise decreased from 2.9 to 2.3. During this period, both values remained substantially stable in the overall economy.
### Comparative Analysis of Business Structure
The structural transformation highlighted by the data from the Federal Statistical Office shows how the entrepreneurial fabric of culture is evolving towards a pulverization into more agile entities but with lesser overall employment strength. The contraction of full-time equivalents (FTEs) from 2.9 to 2.3 per enterprise between 2011 and 2024 reflects a labor fragmentation dynamic that contrasts with the stability recorded by the Swiss economy as a whole.
The variation across different branches highlights divergent dynamics: while advertising and the audiovisual and multimedia sector are growing with marked increases of +6.3% and +6.5%, traditional sectors such as books and printing are undergoing prolonged structural reductions, culminating in a 12.3% drop compared to 2019. Regarding older workers, identified in the age group between 50 and 64, the number of unemployed increased by 109 units, equal to 0.3% compared to the previous month, for a total value of 38,745 people. Comparing this figure with the same month of the previous year, an increase of 3,105 people is noted, corresponding to 8.7%. In July 2026, the unemployment rate of older workers stood at 2.7%, recording an increase of 0.1 percentage points compared to the previous month. At the same time, the total number of job seekers registered was 227,200, with an increase of 1,409 people compared to the previous month, equal to 0.6%. Compared to the previous year, the increase in job seekers is 17,759 units, or 8.5%. The job seekers rate remained stable at 4.8% in July 2026. Net of seasonal variations, job seekers increased by 2,281 units (+1%) compared to the previous month, reaching 238,134, while the corresponding seasonally adjusted rate remained unchanged at 5.0%. The analysis of the data provided by SECO for the month of July 2026 also allows for a careful examination of the situation regarding job vacancies and the phenomenon of short-time work in Switzerland. In detail, the job vacancies announced at the ORCs in July 2026 amounted to 45,156, registering a decrease of 2,088 units compared to the previous month, equal to -4.4%. Of these, 29,738 positions, representing 65.9% of the total, are subject to the notification obligation. Compared to the same period of the previous year, there is an increase of 5,351 job vacancies, equal to 13.4%. Net of seasonal variations, for the month of July 2026 there is a decrease in job vacancies equal to 275 units, or -0.6% compared to the previous month, for a total of 43,244. Regarding the exhaustion of the right to unemployment benefits, the data available at the end of July 2026 indicate that the persons who exhausted this right in May 2026 were 2,629. This is 46 more people, equal to an increase of 1.8% compared to April 2026. Due to the payment practice, unemployment fund data relating to the exhaustion of rights and short-time work are published with a delay of two to three months and may be subject to subsequent changes.
### The short-time work sector
Another significant element emerging from the surveys concerns the recourse to short-time work. According to the data available at the end of July 2026, in April 2026 the people affected by short-time work were 9,782, registering a decrease of 328 people, equal to -3.2% compared to the month of March 2026, against a registration period of three months. From the same registration period, it appears that the business sectors involved are 41 less, with a reduction of -5.7% compared to March 2026, for a total of 673 sectors affected. Experience shows that short-time work recorded after three months stands at around 75 percent of the provisional total. These data highlight how the Swiss labor market is facing various cyclical dynamics, reflecting economic fluctuations in the different productive sectors and offering a useful framework for monitoring employment stability at the national level.

item.title: Transalpine freight traffic: data and growth in 2026
item.description: Growth in transalpine freight traffic of 3.1% in the first half of 2026. The share of the railroad stands at 68%, while trucks are growing.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Growth of transalpine freight traffic by 3.1% in the first half of 2026 - Railway market share at 68%, down by 0.9 percentage points - Increase in road transport and truck journeys reaching 511,000 - Single wagonload freight traffic recorded an 8% decline
## Key facts - **What**: Federal Office of Transport semi-annual reports on freight traffic - When: First half of 2026 - Where: Switzerland, transalpine and north-south axis - Who: Federal Office of Transport and Federal Council - Amount: 12 million franc loss for SBB Cargo in single wagonload freight
In the first half of 2026, Swiss railways transported a higher volume of goods through the Alps compared to the corresponding period of the previous year. According to reports published in Bern by the Federal Office of Transport, the growth recorded by the railway sector stands at 3.1 percent. Despite this growth, the increase in road transport proved to be significantly higher, leading to a slight contraction in the railway's market share in transalpine freight traffic, which now stands at 68 percent.
Both rail and road benefited from a favorable economic environment and an expanding overall market during the first six months of the year. However, truck journeys grew by approximately 7 percent, reaching 511,000. Based on this trend, projections indicate that by the end of 2026 the annual number of trips made by trucks will once again exceed one million, a milestone that has not been recorded for a long time in the heavy road transport sector across Swiss territory.
### Critical issues on the north-south axis
An element of severe pressure for rail freight traffic remains the numerous construction sites along the north-south axis, the negative impact of which is felt particularly in Germany. The complex infrastructural situation limits the fluidity of rail connections, and competent authorities estimate that an effective improvement will not materialize before around 2030. To counteract these difficulties and support the sector, the Federal Council has included additional financial resources within the current revision of the freight transport law, specifically aimed at boosting rail freight traffic through the Alps.
At the same time, single wagonload freight transport, which represents an essential pillar for domestic, import, and export logistics nationwide, is going through a phase of operational contraction. During the first six months of 2026, the number of loaded wagons used in this mode showed an 8 percent decrease compared to data recorded in the same period of the previous year, while costs per single wagon stabilized. The analysis of the half-yearly data published by the Federal Office of Transport highlights divergent dynamics between the different modes of freight transport in Switzerland, reflecting the reactivity of the market in the face of cyclical and structural factors. On the one hand, the rubber sector benefits from greater immediate operational flexibility, which has allowed it to absorb demand growth with an increase in truck runs of 7 percent. On the other hand, the railway meets the structural limits deriving from international shipyards and the congestion of the foreign network, in particular German, which penalize the competitiveness of north-south transits along the Alpine routes.
The Confederation actively intervenes to support the railway sector through targeted subsidies, as in the case of isolated wagon traffic, for which constant semi-annual monitoring has been introduced. Despite the public indemnities paid in the reference period, SBB Cargo closed the first half of 2026 with a negative economic result in the sector of isolated complete wagon transport, registering a loss of 12 million francs compared to 40 million francs of financial support received. This economic scenario highlights the complexity of keeping a fundamental service in balance for the capillarity of internal and foreign logistics without placing an excessive burden on company balance sheets.

item.description: The Ticino cantonal initiative becomes a federal bill for ultra-broadband throughout the national territory.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - 365 million francs allocated by the government - Resources distributed over an eight-year period - Coverage extended to the entire national territory - Universal service brought to 80 Mbps from 2024
## Key facts - * * What * *: Ultra Broadband Bill - When: ITER started in 2016, updated in 2023 and 2024 - Where: Swiss Confederation and outlying regions - Who: Federal Council and Federal Chambers - Amount: CHF 365 million
The Federal Council has decided to implement with a specific proposal for a law the cantonal initiative originally presented by the national socialist councilor Bruno Storni, entitled 'Guaranteeing a widespread offer of ultra-broadband services throughout the national territory'. The announcement was made by Bruno Storni himself through a post on the Facebook social platform, highlighting the arrival of positive news directly from Bern for digital connectivity in Switzerland. The total appropriation budgeted by the federal government amounts to 365 million francs, a figure that will be gradually spread and disbursed over eight years to support the less densely populated areas of the country.
### Origins of the cantonal initiative
The measure has its roots in a cantonal initiative formalized in Ticino in 2015, which made an explicit request for widespread coverage of ultra-broadband services extended to the entire Swiss national territory. The technological and regulatory evolution linked to this digitisation plan has seen fundamental milestones in recent years. Already in 2023, the federal authorities adopted the so-called 'Gigabit Strategy', a programmatic approach aimed at guaranteeing a connection speed of at least 1 Gbit/s in download through the fixed network connections available in the territory. At the same time, following the long parliamentary process, the Confederation has decided to increase the level of mandatory universal service to 80 Mbps from 2024. This technical threshold currently places the Swiss network among the highest levels internationally in terms of the provision of basic telecommunications infrastructure.
### The current legislative process
The transformation of the cantonal initiative into an organic law text represents the next crucial institutional step. The regulatory package prepared by the Federal Council is now submitted to the formal examination of the Federal Chambers, which will have to debate, evaluate and possibly approve the operational and financial details of the measure before its definitive entry into force in the Swiss regulatory system.

The use of the 365 million francs allocated by the federal government will allow the strengthening of fixed and mobile network infrastructures in territories characterized by lower population densities or particular morphological difficulties. Those who reside or work outside the main urban centres will gradually benefit from more stable, faster internet connections aligned with the parameters of the aforementioned 'Gigabit Strategy'.

## In breve - Sostegno mensile per figli e giovani in formazione nel Canton Giura - Gestione tramite cassa di compensazione competente - Procedura di domanda basata su condizioni di diritto specifiche - Importi differenziati tra assegni familiari e di formazione
## Fatti chiave - **Cosa**: Assegni familiari e di formazione - Dove: Canton Giura - Chi: Genitori/tutori con figli a carico - Importo: Definito dalle scale cantonali (non ancora specificato nel dettaglio) - Ente: Cassa di compensazione competente
Il sistema di previdenza sociale svizzera prevede, nel Canton Giura, l'erogazione di assegni familiari volti a sostenere i costi legati alla crescita e all'istruzione dei figli. Questi contributi rappresentano un pilastro fondamentale per l'economia domestica dei residenti, integrando il reddito salariale attraverso trasferimenti diretti gestiti dalle casse di compensazione. L'accesso a tali prestazioni non è automatico, ma richiede la verifica di precise condizioni di diritto legate alla residenza, al legame di parentela e all'età dei beneficiari.
### Tipologie di assegni previsti Nel Canton Giura si distinguono principalmente due categorie di prestazioni. Gli assegni familiari sono destinati ai figli fino al raggiungimento di una determinata soglia d'età, mentre gli assegni di formazione intervengono quando il giovane prosegue gli studi o intraprende un apprendistato, estendendo il periodo di sostegno finanziario. Questa distinzione assicura che il supporto economico sia allineato alle effettive necessità della famiglia, che variano significativamente tra l'infanzia e l'adolescenza.
L'erogazione di questi importi è strettamente legata alla normativa cantonale, che definisce le soglie di accesso e le modalità di calcolo. Poiché ogni Cantone gestisce autonomamente le proprie scale di importi, è essenziale fare riferimento agli aggiornamenti della cassa di compensazione di riferimento per conoscere le cifre esatte applicate nell'anno in corso. La gestione amministrativa segue i principi della previdenza sociale svizzera, coordinandosi con le istituzioni federali come l'UFAS/BSV per quanto riguarda i quadri normativi generali della previdenza. ## Analisi delle condizioni di diritto L'ottenimento degli assegni familiari nel Canton Giura dipende dal soddisfacimento di criteri rigorosi. Il richiedente deve dimostrare il legame di parentela o di tutela legale nei confronti del figlio. Un aspetto cruciale riguarda la residenza e l'attività lavorativa: i diritti agli assegni sono generalmente legati all'essere soggetti all'obbligo contributivo AVS/AHV nel territorio svizzero o, in specifici casi coordinati, in base agli accordi internazionali per chi risiede all'estero ma lavora in Svizzera.
### Scenari di formazione e istruzione Un'implicazione pratica rilevante riguarda il passaggio dagli assegni familiari a quelli di formazione. In uno scenario ipotetico, un giovane che completa l'obbligo scolastico e inizia un percorso di formazione professionale continua a generare un diritto al sostegno finanziario per i genitori. Questo meccanismo evita che l'uscita dal sistema scolastico primario causi un'improvvisa interruzione del supporto economico, facilitando l'inserimento nel mercato del lavoro attraverso l'apprendistato.
Il costo della vita in Svizzera, che incide pesantemente su affitti e assicurazioni malattia LAMal/KVG, rende questi assegni un elemento di stabilità. Sebbene l'importo non copra l'intera spesa di mantenimento, esso contribuisce a mitigare l'impatto finanziario delle spese scolastiche e dei materiali didattici. È utile confrontare questi importi con le deduzioni fiscali disponibili nella dichiarazione delle imposte tax-return, poiché gli assegni familiari possono influenzare il calcolo del reddito imponibile a seconda delle leggi cantonali e comunali vigenti nel Giura.
L'interazione tra previdenza e fiscalità è un punto chiave: mentre l'assegno è un beneficio previdenziale, la sua gestione richiede una documentazione accurata che deve essere presentata annualmente o al variare delle condizioni familiari. La precisione nella dichiarazione dei dati evita rimborsi retroattivi o sanzioni per indebiti percepiti, garantendo un flusso di cassa costante per il nucleo familiare.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## Procedura di domanda e iter amministrativo Per richiedere gli assegni familiari nel Canton Giura, il primo passo consiste nell'identificare la cassa di compensazione competente. Solitamente, per i lavoratori dipendenti, la domanda viene inoltrata tramite il datore di lavoro, che funge da intermediario tra il dipendente e l'ente previdenziale. Per i lavoratori indipendenti, la domanda va presentata direttamente alla cassa di compensazione a cui sono affiliati per i contributi AVS/AHV.
### Documentazione necessaria e step operativi La procedura richiede la compilazione di un modulo ufficiale di domanda. I documenti solitamente richiesti includono: - Certificato di nascita del figlio o prova del legame di parentela - Attestati di studio o contratto di apprendistato per gli assegni di formazione - Documenti d'identità validi - Eventuali certificati di residenza se richiesti dall'ente
Una volta presentata la domanda, la cassa di compensazione verifica i requisiti di diritto. In caso di esito positivo, l'importo viene versato mensilmente. È fondamentale segnalare tempestivamente qualsiasi cambiamento nella situazione familiare (come la nascita di un nuovo figlio o il termine degli studi di un giovane) per aggiornare l'importo dell'assegno.
Per chi desidera pianificare il budget familiare includendo queste entrate, è consigliabile utilizzare strumenti di calcolo per stimare il reddito netto mensile. Considerare l'impatto di questi assegni insieme agli altri costi fissi, come i premi della cassa malati o i contributi LPP/BVG, permette una gestione finanziaria più accurata. Per una stima completa delle entrate mensili, è possibile utilizzare il nostro [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator), che aiuta a visualizzare l'impatto delle detrazioni e dei benefici sul salario netto.
⚠️ Ricordate che le scadenze per l'invio della domanda e i termini di prescrizione per le richieste retroattive sono definiti dalla legge cantonale e federale; pertanto, l'invio tempestivo della documentazione è l'unico modo per garantire la ricezione dei fondi a partire dalla data di maturazione del diritto.

item.title: Vaud sick pay premiums: how to get the reduction
item.description: Deductibles, alternative models and cantonal subsidy requirements: a practical guide to LAMal awards in the Canton of Vaud.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - LAMal obbligatoria per tutti i residenti, premi pro capite - Franchigie adulti da 300 a 2500 franchi - Riduzione premi è un sussidio cantonale, non automatico - Domanda va inoltrata all'ente cantonale competente
## Fatti chiave - **Cosa**: Assicurazione malattia obbligatoria (LAMal) nel Canton Vaud - Quando: Da stipulare entro 3 mesi dall'arrivo in Svizzera - Dove: Cantone di Vaud, con premi regionali - Chi: Tutti i residenti, con riduzione premi per redditi bassi - Importo: Franchigie da CHF 300 a CHF 2500 per adulti
Il Cantone di Vaud, come tutti i cantoni svizzeri, applica la legge federale sull'assicurazione malattia (LAMal). Ogni residente deve stipulare una copertura di base entro tre mesi dall'arrivo. Il premio è individuale e varia per cantone e regione, non è una tassa né un contributo salariale, ma un costo diretto a carico dell'assicurato.
La scelta della franchigia è uno dei fattori che incide maggiormente sul premio. Per gli adulti, le opzioni vanno da 300 a 2500 franchi all'anno. Chi sceglie una franchigia più alta paga premi mensili più bassi, ma in caso di cure deve coprire personalmente una quota maggiore di spese. I modelli alternativi (come il medico di famiglia o il teleconsulto) permettono di ridurre ulteriormente il costo del premio, vincolando l'assicurato a determinate modalità di accesso alle cure.
### Il sistema a tre livelli La sanità svizzera si basa su una ripartizione chiara di competenze: la Confederazione definisce il quadro legale, i cantoni gestiscono l'assicurazione malattia e la riduzione dei premi, mentre i comuni non hanno un ruolo diretto in questo ambito. L'Ufficio federale della sanità pubblica (UFSP) supervisiona il sistema, ma non fissa i premi, che sono determinati dalle casse malati sulla base dei costi sanitari regionali.
Per chi ha un reddito modesto, esiste la riduzione dei premi: un sussidio cantonale che abbassa l'importo mensile da pagare. I requisiti dipendono dal reddito e dalla sostanza, e la domanda va presentata all'ente cantonale competente. Nel Canton Vaud, come altrove, la riduzione non è automatica: va richiesta ogni anno e viene calcolata sulla base della situazione fiscale dell'assicurato. ## Analisi pratica: come scegliere e risparmiare La scelta della franchigia è una decisione che va valutata con attenzione. Un adulto sano che non prevede spese mediche elevate può optare per una franchigia di 2500 franchi, riducendo il premio mensile in modo significativo. Al contrario, chi ha bisogno di cure regolari (fisioterapia, farmaci cronici, visite specialistiche) potrebbe trovarsi a spendere di più se sceglie una franchigia alta, perché deve coprire personalmente le prime spese fino al raggiungimento dell'importo.
I modelli alternativi sono un'altra leva per contenere i costi. Il modello del medico di famiglia, ad esempio, richiede di rivolgersi sempre al proprio medico di base, che poi indirizza agli specialisti. Il modello teleconsulto prevede di contattare prima un centro telefonico. Questi modelli offrono premi ridotti, ma impongono un percorso di cura più rigido. Nel Canton Vaud, come nel resto della Svizzera, le casse malati pubblicano i premi per ciascun modello e ciascuna franchigia, permettendo un confronto diretto.
### Prima e dopo: cosa cambia con la riduzione premi La riduzione dei premi è un meccanismo che esiste da decenni, ma i criteri di eleggibilità vengono aggiornati periodicamente. Chi ha diritto al sussidio lo riceve sotto forma di sconto diretto sul premio mensile, oppure come rimborso annuale, a seconda delle modalità del cantone. Senza la domanda, il sussidio non viene concesso: è responsabilità dell'assicurato presentare la richiesta entro i termini stabiliti.
Per chi arriva in Svizzera per lavoro, la questione è particolarmente rilevante. Il salario lordo non tiene conto dei premi, che vanno pagati separatamente. In un cantone con premi medi come Vaud, il costo mensile può incidere in modo significativo sul bilancio familiare. Per questo, conviene verificare subito se si ha diritto alla riduzione, presentando la domanda all'ufficio cantonale competente, solitamente collegato al servizio delle contribuzioni.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## How to get the reduction: step-by-step procedure 1. **Check requirements**: Premium reduction depends on taxable income and substance. Check the Canton of Vaud's website for updated income limits. 2. Prepare the documentation: You will need the last tax return, if already filed, or an income estimate if you have just arrived. 3. Submit the application: The application is submitted to the cantonal body in charge, usually via an online or paper form. The expiry is typically within a certain period from the beginning of the insurance year. 4. Wait for the decision: The office evaluates your situation and communicates the amount of the subsidy, which will be deducted from the monthly premiums. 5. Renew every year: The reduction is not automatic: it must be requested again every year, based on the updated tax situation.
If you have any doubts about the deductible or the most suitable model, use our [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator) to understand how much the premium affects your net income. To compare health insurance offers, you can use the [comparatore LAMal](nav:health). And if you're considering moving to another canton, keep in mind that the premiums vary: the [costo della vita](nav:cost-of-living) in Switzerland also depends on this factor.
Do not wait: the premium reduction is a right that must be exercised. A late application may result in the loss of the grant for the current year.

## In brief - Ordinary naturalization in St. Gallen requires integration and language tests - There is a naturalization fee to be paid - The procedure can take several months, depending on the municipality
## Key Facts - **What**: years requirements, integration test, language, fees - Where: Canton of St. Gallen, municipality of residence - Who: applicant with C permit - Amount: naturalization fee (not yet specified)
The Canton of St. Gallen has published guidelines for ordinary naturalization. The procedure is divided into several stages: the applicant must prove that he or she has lived for a period determined by both the canton and the municipality of residence, pass an integration test and a language test, and pay the required fees. The necessary residence permit is the C permit, which is usually obtained after ten years of residence (with a double count for the years between the 8th and 18th).
The cantonal and municipal authorities work together to check the residence time requirements: the canton sets a minimum number of years, while the municipality can request an additional period. Only after meeting these criteria can the applicant access the integration test, which assesses knowledge of Swiss culture, institutions and norms. At the same time, it is mandatory to pass the language test, which varies depending on the level required by the municipality.
Once the applicant has passed the tests, he or she must pay the naturalization fee. The amount varies depending on the canton and municipality, but it is a fixed item in the procedure. After payment, the application is reviewed by the municipality, which forwards the file to the canton. The total time, from the submission of the application to the granting of citizenship, can extend to several months, depending on how quickly the municipality completes the documentary verification.
> "The new cantonal legislation establishes that citizenship is not granted if the integration requirements are not fully met".
### National tax environment The Swiss tax system has three levels of taxation – federal, cantonal and municipal – and each canton applies its own multiplier. The naturalisation tax is also part of the cantonal component, so it is advisable to check the exact amount with the tax office in your municipality. For more details on the tax return, please consult the tax-return service. ## Practical analysis The naturalization process in St. Gallen has concrete implications for those who live and work in Switzerland. First of all, the requirement of years of residence imposes long-term planning: those who have just obtained a C permit must take into account that the counting of years begins from the moment the permit is issued and that, for individuals between 8 and 18 years of age, the years count double. This can reduce the time it takes to reach the cantonal threshold, but at the same time requires a careful verification of the periods recognized by the municipality.
The integration test, although not specified in detail, is a common element in all cantons. Its assessment includes knowledge of Swiss democratic institutions, the values of neutrality and the system of direct democracy. Preparation may require specific courses offered by cantonal bodies or private schools. At the same time, the language test is essential: the canton of St. Gallen requires mastery of German, with a level that varies depending on the municipality. Those coming from a French-speaking or Italian-speaking area will have to invest time in language courses to meet this requirement.
From an economic point of view, the naturalization fee represents an additional cost. Although the amount is not indicated, it is an expense to be included in the family budget, especially for those who already have commitments related to direct federal taxes, VAT and AHV/AHV contributions. In addition, the duration of the procedure – several months – means that applicants will have to maintain full KVG insurance coverage throughout the process, since citizenship does not alter insurance status.
A comparison with other cantons shows that St. Gallen follows the national logic but may differ in terms of the number of years required by the municipality and the amount of the tax. If you have already started the procedure in another canton, you should check whether the periods of residence already accrued are recognized by St. Gallen, otherwise you may have to supplement additional years. This is crucial for professionals who change their domicile for business reasons.
### Impact on the labour market Holding Swiss citizenship can facilitate access to public jobs and certain categories of employment that require citizenship. In addition, citizenship eliminates the need to periodically renew one's residence permit, reducing administrative uncertainty for employees and employers. For those interested in assessing the impact on their paycheck, the [payslip](nav:payslip) calculator can provide an estimate of AHV/AHV, BVG and other deductions after obtaining citizenship.

Calculate the years of residence: count the years of presence in Switzerland since the C permit was issued; remember that the years between 8 and 18 count double. If the total does not yet reach the cantonal minimum, continue to reside regularly. 3. Gather documentation: integration certificates, language certificate (German), extracts from the population register, proof of payment of fees, and any employment certificates. All documents must be translated into German if necessary and notarized. 4. Submit the application to the municipality: send the complete dossier to the competent municipal office. The municipality will carry out an initial check and may request additions. 5. Take the tests: Take the integration test and the language test organized by the canton or municipality. Prepare yourself with specific courses or teaching materials provided by the authorities. 6. Pay the naturalisation fee: pay the amount required by the canton; keep the receipt for the next step. 7. Wait for the cantonal decision: the canton examines the file, verifies the results of the tests and the regularity of the payments. The response time varies, but it is normal to wait several months. 8. Final registration: Once citizenship has been granted, register your new status with the tax office and update your KVG insurance.
Throughout the process, it is advisable to keep an eye on tax and contribution deadlines. To assess the impact of citizenship on the overall tax burden, use our calculator dedicated to taxes and social contributions.

item.description: Uniform federal legal framework, maximum deposit 3 months, cancellation only on official form, dispute within 30 days to the conciliation authority.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - Identical federal lease right in all cantons (CO art. 253 et seq.) - Maximum security deposit of 3 months on a restricted account in the name of the tenant - Lessor's cancellation valid only on official cantonal form - Dispute initial fee within 30 days to the conciliation authority
## Key facts - **What**: Federal Rules on Deposit, Cancellation and Rent Dispute - When: Valid without expiry, applicable to each new contract - Where: Canton of St. Gallen and all of Switzerland - Who: Cantonal landlords, tenants, conciliation authorities - Amount: Deposit max 3 rents; cancellation terms 1/2/3 months for seniority
The right to rent in Switzerland is governed at the federal level by the Code of Obligations (CO art. 253 et seq.) and applies identically in the Canton of St. Gallen as in the rest of the country. This means that the rules on security deposit, form of cancellation and contestation of the initial fee do not vary from one canton to another.
### Security deposit and escrow account The law sets a maximum limit: the deposit cannot exceed three months' rent (including ancillary charges). The sum must be paid into a restricted account in the tenant's name with a Swiss bank; the landlord cannot dispose of it freely. Upon termination of the contract, the deposit plus interest is returned except for established credits of the lessor (damages, arrears of rent).
