Since federal law is uniform, the difference is made by rent levels, which vary between cities (St. Gallen, Rapperswil-Jona, Wil) and suburban municipalities, as well as between new and old buildings.
A tenant who signs a contract for a 3.5 premises in the central area must know that the required deposit cannot exceed three monthly rentals. If the landlord asks for four months or a payment on his own account, the request is illegitimate. Similarly, a cancellation received on plain paper or via WhatsApp has no legal value: only the official cantonal form is authentic.
### Comparison with other cantons: same right, different markets Unlike taxation (where each canton sets its own multiplier and rates), the right to rent knows no cantonal differences. However, the conciliation authorities are organized at the cantonal level: in the Canton of St. Gallen, the "Schlichtungsbehörden in Miet- und Pachtsachen" established in the districts are responsible. The procedure, deadlines and forms may have slight formal variations, but the substantive principles (30-day deadline, burden of proof, benchmarks) remain the federal ones.

item.title: Young people in Ticino: demographic analysis and USTAT flows
item.description: USTAT demographic analysis on young people in Ticino: negative intercantonal balance towards other cantons but offset by new arrivals from abroad.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Ticino is not aging thanks to immigration - More 25-35 year-olds arrive than leave - The intercantonal balance towards other Cantons is negative - Those who study north of the Alps return in 55% of cases
## Key facts - **What**: Demographic analysis on young people and migration - When: September 11, 2026 - Where: Canton of Ticino - Who: Cantonal Office of Statistics (USTAT) - Age: 25-35 year-olds - Annual average: 495 people lost to other Cantons - Source: USTAT analysis and interview with Francesco Giudici
Despite Ticino losing its young people, the population is not aging thanks to the fundamental contribution of immigration. This is revealed by data from a recent analysis conducted by the Cantonal Office of Statistics (USTAT) and explored in an interview with Francesco Giudici, head of the USTAT Society Sector. The survey focuses on the 25 to 35 age group, outlining a complex but not unexpected picture for the cantonal territory.
### Migration dynamics and balances Going into the detail of the numbers published by the Cantonal Office of Statistics, the overall migration balance for young people is positive. In other words, more 25 and 35-year-olds arrive than leave the cantonal territory. However, analyzing the direction of the flows, a critical issue emerges in movements within the Confederation. Between 2015 and 2024, the intercantonal balance proved negative, recording an average loss of 495 people per year heading towards other Swiss cantons. A significant part of this internal mobility has the city of Zurich as its final destination, attractive for professional and educational opportunities.
### The role of new arrivals Those who leave often find a new dimension north of the Alps, while those replacing the departing residents are mainly citizens coming from abroad, particularly from Italy. Statistical analysis confirms that the vast majority of those arriving in Ticino from across the borders come from the neighboring country, widely exceeding the departures recorded in the same period. This phenomenon compensates for the youth demographic loss, fitting into a broader context of cross-border and international labor mobility that has historically characterized the canton's economy and local labor market. The demographic dynamics analysed by the Cantonal Statistical Office (USTAT) offer important insights for the economic and social future of Ticino, especially when compared with forecasts on population ageing. Historically considered a Canton with a strong elderly component, Ticino faces structural challenges related to workforce management and territorial competitiveness. The Federal Statistical Office (FSO/SBB) predicts that, with the progressive retirement of baby boomers, competition to attract young workers between Switzerland and the European Union will intensify pressure on local markets.
### The demographic challenge in Lombardy and Italy A crucial aspect highlighted by the analysis concerns the fact that demographic ageing does not represent an exclusively Ticino peculiarity. Similar dynamics are also recorded in the neighbouring regions, starting from Lombardy and the Italian territory. This means that in the future even the territories of origin of migratory flows could be activated to retain the young local generations, potentially reducing the availability of a skilled workforce ready to move or work in the Confederation. Competition for young talent will therefore become a determining factor for cantonal businesses and administrations.

item.title: Seasonal in Tourism: Featured Accommodation Expenses
item.description: A study by the University of Lausanne commissioned by the Federal Office of Housing analyzes the housing difficulties of seasonal workers.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - University of Lausanne study on seasonal workers - Commissioned by the Federal Housing Office - 95 interviews conducted in 4 tourist destinations - Housing expenses indicated as the main difficulty
## Key facts - What: Analysis of the housing situation of seasonal workers - When: September 11, 2026 - Where: Adelboden, Leysin, Saas-Fee and Villars-sur-Ollon - Who: University of Lausanne and Federal Housing Office - Amount: 95 total interviews, of which 84 with seasonal workers - Context: Co-financed by the Cantons of Bern, Vaud and Valais
The Swiss tourism sector cannot do without seasonal workers, but their presence is closely linked to the availability of adequate living spaces. A recent study conducted by the University of Lausanne, commissioned by the Federal Housing Office and co-financed by the Cantons of Bern, Vaud and Valais, has analyzed for the first time the housing situation from the perspective of seasonal workers. The report, entitled «Usages et besoins en logement des travailleurs saisonniers en stations de sports d'hiver», highlights the main problem encountered in this economic sector: housing expenses.
In Swiss alpine localities, rising rental prices heavily impact the budgets of temporary employees, whose cantonal minimum salaries average between 3,800 and 4,200 gross Swiss francs per month according to the collective employment agreements of the hotel and catering industry (L-GAV).
### Methodology and scope of the research Research is based on a total of 95 interviews, including 84 conducted directly with seasonal workers employed in the destinations of Adelboden, Leysin, Saas-Fee and Villars-sur-Ollon. Living spaces play a central role not only for the daily life of these people, but decisively influence the possibility of finding a job, the individual financial situation and the eventual decision to return to work in a specific tourist resort. The presence of an adequate housing supply therefore represents a crucial factor for tourist destinations, useful for attracting labor and retaining it over the long term, ensuring the operational continuity of local businesses.
> The housing crisis in tourist valleys directly threatens the competitiveness of our hotel and non-hotel system.
### Practical scenarios and financial impact In Saas-Fee and Adelboden, a standard studio apartment for the winter season can exceed 1,200 francs per month, absorbing up to thirty percent of the net salary of an unskilled seasonal worker. To make a comparison with urban centers like Zurich or Geneva, where cost per square meter is high but offset by higher average salaries, in tourist resorts the ratio between fixed rental costs and seasonal income of 4-5 months creates a structural savings deficit for foreign employees or inter-cantonal commuters. Companies that provide company housing at subsidized prices, often obtained from old annexes or converted hotel rooms, record staff retention rates forty-five percent higher than those who leave workers free to find a roof on the free alpine real estate market. Analyzing the housing needs that emerged from the interviews, industry operators and local authorities are facing well-defined priorities indicated by workers. The research highlights that finding affordable housing represents the absolute need. High housing costs relative to income drastically reduce the possibility of setting aside savings during the season. In Graubünden and Valais, where the average cost of a studio apartment often exceeds 1'200 Swiss francs per month, seasonal workers who earn a gross minimum salary of around 3'800 francs according to the Collective Employment Agreement for the hotel and catering industry find themselves allocating over 35% of their income solely to rent. In addition to the economic factor, seasonal workers express the need to find housing solutions close to their workplace and the essential services of the location. Short routes simplify everyday life and reduce costs related to mobility, a particularly relevant aspect if one considers the sometimes irregular working hours typical of winter tourism and the adverse weather conditions of the cold season.
### Qualitative aspects and contractual flexibility As for the furnishings and quality of the housing, the priorities are not linked to high demands for comfort, but rather to cleanliness, adequate sizes, complete equipment and the possibility of enjoying a minimum of privacy. This need proves crucial in shared accommodation, where different schedules and life rhythms can complicate daily coexistence between colleagues. The fourth priority identified by the study concerns the flexibility of lease contracts. Often the duration of rental agreements does not coincide with that of the seasonal employment contract, generating unjustified additional costs for workers. Interviewees hope for flexible lease start and end dates and the possibility of re-renting the same accommodation in subsequent seasons, thus stabilizing the presence of workers in the alpine valleys.
- Rent commensurate with the cantonal minimum wage - Maximum distance of fifteen minutes on foot from the ski lifts - Minimum equipment with independent kitchen and internet connection included
> The stabilization of the workforce necessarily passes through a farsighted housing policy for the tourist valleys.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). The housing situation for seasonal workers in the Swiss tourism sector varies considerably depending on the location, highlighting marked disparities between the various Alpine centers of the Confederation. The ease of finding suitable accommodation depends on critical factors such as local availability and prices, the percentage of secondary residences in the area pursuant to the Federal Act on Second Homes (L2H) which entered into force in 2016, the accessibility of transport links, and the housing supply available in neighboring municipalities.
Analyzing regional data, in locations such as Zermatt (Canton of Valais) or St. Moritz (Canton of Graubünden), where the real estate market is under severe pressure, costs for a single room for seasonal workers can easily exceed 900-1200 Swiss francs per month, heavily impacting gross salaries which, according to the Collective Employment Agreements (CEA) for the hotel and catering industry (L-GAV), generally range between 3850 and 4400 francs per month for staff without specific qualifications. Conversely, in peripheral valleys of Ticino or in smaller resorts of the Bernese Oberland, average prices often range between 550 and 750 francs, while still facing issues related to the aging of properties.
Workshops organized in the four examined destinations and discussions at the national level have demonstrated that there is no single solution valid everywhere, but rather the need to develop approaches tailored to local specificities.
### Operational measures for employers and Municipalities - Advance planning of bed requirements at least 6 months before the season - Conversion of commercial properties or disused hotels into employee residences - Establishment of long-term agreements with local owners to freeze rental fees - Sharing of housing resources among multiple companies in the same tourist destination
Employers and Municipalities are called upon to act in close collaboration with the Cantons, tourist organizations, and other local economic actors to develop concrete responses. The report by the University of Lausanne offers a practical working basis with various intervention possibilities, including tax reliefs for companies investing in the construction of staff housing and municipal building incentives that derogate from normal utilization rates.
### How to explore the economic and employment situation in depth For those operating in the Swiss labor market and wishing to evaluate their economic position, the impact of fixed expenses on income, or available professional opportunities, it is useful to consult the economic analysis tools made available online. Verifying the impact of the cost of living, mandatory social deductions (AHV/IV/EO, ALV, BVG), and salaries makes it possible to better plan any transfer or professional commitment in the different regions of the Confederation.

item.description: SCNAT warns: springs dry up in the Jura and the Alps. Monitoring and renaturalization are needed to protect the groundwater.
item.content:encoded:
## In short - Drought threatens Switzerland's water supply, with 80% of drinking water coming from underground sources. - Experts propose monitoring, renaturalization of watercourses and territorial planning. - Collaboration between the Confederation, Cantons and user sectors is essential to manage the crisis.
## Key facts - **What**: Drought in Switzerland, risk for groundwater - When: Not yet specified - Where: Switzerland, with focus on the Jura and the Alps - Who: Swiss Academy of Natural Sciences (SCNAT) - Amount: 150 cubic kilometers of groundwater in Switzerland
Drought is becoming a recurring challenge in Switzerland, putting at risk 80% of the country's drinking water, which comes from underground sources. The Swiss Academy of Natural Sciences (SCNAT) is sounding the alarm: groundwater levels are falling and springs are drying up, especially in the Jura and the Alps. This situation can cause water shortages for families, agriculture and industry, as well as threatening water quality with higher concentrations of pollutants.
### Measures proposed by experts Experts propose various measures to address the crisis: systematic monitoring of water withdrawals, replenishment of aquifers through the removal of soil sealing and renaturalization of waterways. These solutions should be integrated into spatial planning.
SCNAT highlights the importance of close collaboration between the Confederation, cantons, municipalities, distribution companies, the agricultural sector and other user groups for effective responses. The impact of drought varies from region to region: the large aquifers of the Plateau can act as a buffer, while in the Jura and the Alps the sources can run out quickly.
The situation requires immediate action to ensure the resilience of Swiss water resources. Spatial planning and sustainable water management are key to addressing this recurring challenge. Agriculture, which is highly dependent on water resources, could suffer significant losses, impacting food production and prices of agricultural products.
### Sectors affected - **Agriculture**: Reduction of crops and increase in irrigation costs. - Industry: Increase in energy and production costs due to water scarcity. - Families: Possible rationing and increase in water tariffs.
Water quality is another critical aspect. As groundwater levels decline, pollutants can concentrate, making water undrinkable without additional treatment. This could increase costs for distribution companies and, consequently, household bills.
### Long-term solutions Renaturalizing waterways and removing soil sealing are long-term solutions that can help restore ecosystems and ensure a sustainable water supply. However, these measures require significant investments and careful planning.
Collaboration between various levels of government and use sectors is crucial. The Confederation, cantons and municipalities must work together to implement effective policies and ensure that water resources are managed sustainably. item.description: Guide to fees for nurseries, day families and after-school in the Canton of St. Gallen: rates on income, municipal subsidies and tax reductions.

## In a nutshell - Fees calculated on the basis of income and family substance in the individual municipalities - Flexible models between kindergartens (Kita), day families and after-school - Contributions and subsidies paid according to municipal domicile regulations
## Key facts - What * *: Extra-family childcare expenses and reduction contributions - When: Annually at the time of registration and tax update - Where: Canton of St. Gallen and respective municipalities of residence - Who: Families with preschool and school-age children - Amount: Progressive variable fees and tax deductions for custody
The organization of extra-family childcare in the Canton of St. Gallen is one of the central nodes for reconciling professional commitments and domestic life. The Sangallen system is based on cooperation between Cantons, municipal administrations and private managers of preschool educational facilities. Finding an adequate accommodation for the children requires planning in advance, considering the strong impact on the monthly family budget and on the local [costo della vita](nav:cost-of-living) staff.
### Types of educational facilities available In the cantonal territory, families can count on three main channels of reception complementary to the family:

## In brief - Improved financial situation for Swiss hospitals - Over 80% of acute care facilities below the margin - Average EBITDA margin rises to 5.6% but remains insufficient - Strong criticism of the 4% limitation on outpatient costs
## Key facts - **What**: Analysis of the financial situation of Swiss hospitals - When: Last year and forecasts for 2025 - Where: Switzerland - Who: H+, the umbrella association of hospitals, and SpitalBenchmark - Amount: 80% of facilities, average EBITDA margin increased from 4% to 5.6%
The financial situation of Swiss hospitals recorded a slight improvement over the course of last year. Despite this positive sign, the overall context remains particularly tense for the Swiss healthcare sector. According to data released by the hospital umbrella association H+, over 80% of acute care facilities fail to reach the margin necessary to guarantee fully sustainable operations over time. The analysis conducted by the SpitalBenchmark association, which examined over 90% of the hospitals operating in Swiss territory, provides a detailed picture of this transitional phase.
### The trend of operating margins
Looking at the economic data collected by the analysis in detail, the average EBITDA margin of healthcare facilities, calculated by subtracting operating costs from revenues, showed an increase, rising from 4% to 5.6% during 2025. Nonetheless, this percentage level still remains markedly below the 10% threshold deemed essential by experts to ensure solid long-term management. The director of H+, Anne-Geneviève Bütikofer, highlighted how four out of five hospitals are still not generating the essential financial resources needed to make the necessary investments in qualified personnel, new technologies, and adequate infrastructure. Consequently, the Swiss healthcare sector is still a considerable distance away from a genuine structural turnaround. The Swiss hospital sector has reiterated its willingness to decisively strengthen outpatient care, a step considered strategic for effectively containing the overall costs of the national health system. However, healthcare facilities warn that such a radical transformation cannot take place without adequate financial resources and generally favorable framework conditions. The transition towards more modern and sustainable care models indeed requires massive initial investments which, in light of current margins, are difficult for the vast majority of Swiss hospitals to sustain.
### Criticisms of cost growth limitation
Within this complex scenario, the H+ association expressed a markedly critical evaluation of the decisions adopted by the Federal Council. Specifically, it challenges the measure that sets a maximum growth limit of 4% for outpatient costs. According to the estimates and concerns expressed by the hospital sector, a restriction of this magnitude realistically risks halting the transition towards outpatient care. Such a regulatory brake would inevitably end up calling into question the possibility of refinancing future investments, further hindering the path towards a modern and efficient Swiss healthcare system capable of responding to the demographic and economic challenges of the coming years without compromising the quality of services provided to patients residing in the various cantons.

## In brief - Change of presidency at Economiesuisse - Silvan Wildhaber succeeds Christoph Mäder - Full support for the bilateral III agreements
## Key facts - **What**: Change of leadership at the presidency of Economiesuisse - When: Today - Where: Bern - Who: Silvan Wildhaber and Christoph Mäder - Amount: 100,000 companies represented
(Keystone-ATS) The handover took place in Bern during the economy day organized by the association representing Swiss businesses. Economiesuisse has a new leader: after two three-year terms, Christoph Mäder today handed over the presidency to his successor Silvan Wildhaber. During the body's annual general meeting, according to communications from Economiesuisse itself, the new president highlighted the international context. A trade and customs war is raging around us, Wildhaber stated in his speech to the annual assembly, emphasizing that for a small open economy like Switzerland this represents a massive challenge. The 48-year-old added that every opportunity must be seized to improve trade relations, confirming a full commitment to the new free trade agreements with Malaysia and Mercosur, as well as the bilateral III agreements. The entrepreneur from St. Gallen then highlighted the importance of convincing the population of the added value of a strong economy. Companies and their employees create the country's prosperity day after day, offering an indispensable contribution. The outgoing Mäder instead pointed the finger at the stalemate in framework conditions, expressing the hope that Switzerland will once again demonstrate the will to be among the most prosperous countries, with the best educational opportunities, the most sustainable welfare systems, a stable energy supply, and the greatest number of free trade agreements.
### Assembly details and appointments Swiss President Guy Parmelin also spoke at the economy day, emphasizing the importance of diversification in foreign economic policy given global uncertainties, as well as the Chairman of the Governing Board of the Swiss National Bank (SNB) Martin Schlegel, who spoke about his institution's role in guaranteeing stability during a challenging global moment. The assembly elected sixteen new committee members, four of whom also join the steering committee. Among them is Giorgio Pradelli, designated president of the Swiss Bankers Association (SBA), who will assume the vice-presidency of Economiesuisse. The appointment of the new president Wildhaber had instead already taken place on March 16 by the committee. The organization brings together 100 trade associations, 20 cantonal chambers of commerce, and various individual enterprises, representing approximately 100,000 companies from all sectors employing two million people. With substantial resources, the organization seeks to politically influence Switzerland, particularly in federal elections, although not always successfully, as demonstrated by some recent defeats including the Swiss people's vote in favor of the 13th AHV pension. In this context, mention should also be made of the Swiss Trade Association, which also represents businesses but is historically more oriented towards small and medium-sized enterprises compared to Economiesuisse, which is traditionally close to large multinationals and a heavily globally integrated economy. ### Economic priorities and the comparison between organizations
The statements that emerged during the Economiesuisse Economy Day highlight the divergences and complexities that characterize the Swiss entrepreneurial fabric. On the one hand, there is the position of Economiesuisse, focused on defending the interests of large multinationals and global integration through unconditional support for free trade agreements with Malaysia and Mercosur, as well as the bilateral III agreements. On the other hand, the Swiss Arts and Crafts Union operates, led by Council of States member Fabio Regazzi, which represents Swiss small and medium-sized enterprises. This structural distinction means that the positions of the two bodies do not always coincide on crucial issues of economic and federal policy.
### The Swiss political and institutional context
Economiesuisse's action aims to influence the political debate and decisions in Bern with ample financial and organizational resources, although electoral results and popular votes do not always confirm the lines promoted by the association. An emblematic example cited in the recent debate is represented by the popular vote in favor of the thirteenth AVS, which marked a defeat for the positions supported by large economic groups. The reflections expressed by former president Christoph Mäder highlight concern over the blocking of framework conditions, with particular reference to the need for structural reforms in the sectors of education, social security, energy, and international trade agreements. Furthermore, the speech by Confederation President Guy Parmelin reiterated the need for a diversified foreign economic policy to cope with tariff tensions and global trade wars that threaten open economies like Switzerland's. The presence of prominent figures from the financial and institutional world, such as SNB Governing Board President Martin Schlegel, confirms the attention placed on the overall stability of the national economic system in a moment of transition and heightened international challenges.

item.description: The ASIB requires an increase of 2.5% in the wage bill and 2000 francs more for incomes up to 120,000francs for the 2026/2027 negotiations.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - SBEA demands a 2.5% increase in the total salary mass in the banking sector. - An increase of at least 2,000 francs requested for salaries up to 120,000 francs. - Objective: protect purchasing power and share corporate profits. - Transparency required regarding the criteria for distributing salary increases.
## Key facts - **What**: Request for salary adjustments in the Swiss banking sector. - When: Ahead of the 2026/2027 salary negotiations. - Where: Credit institutions operating in Switzerland. - Who: Swiss Bank Employees Association (SBEA). - Amount: Increase of 2,000 francs per year for incomes up to 120,000 francs.
The Swiss Bank Employees Association (SBEA) has formalized its demands for the upcoming salary negotiations, aiming for a 2.5% increase in the total payroll. The claim, decided by the executive committee following discussions with staff representatives, aims to ensure that employees directly participate in the excellent economic results achieved by credit institutions. In addition to the overall percentage, the union specified a minimum threshold of 2,000 additional francs per year for all employees with an annual salary of up to 120,000 francs, calculated on a full-time basis. The SBEA clarified that this request is consistent with the adjustment of minimum wages provided for by the sector's collective labor agreement, which will rise by 2,000 francs starting from January 1, 2027.
### Transparency and distribution criteria A fundamental pillar of the SBEA strategy concerns the request for transparency in corporate decision-making processes. The union demands that banks clearly communicate the criteria used for the distribution of increases, allowing employees and staff representatives to understand the logic behind individual salary variations. The association also suggests that institutions review their salary bands, increasing them where necessary. The recommendation addressed to individual companies is to advance requests of this magnitude while taking into account the specific economic situation and the peculiarities of each individual firm. The ultimate goal remains to ensure that record profits, consistently recorded by various types of banks, from regional ones to large banks like UBS, translate into tangible benefits for the entire workforce that contributes to the institution's operational success. The economic justification put forward by ASIB to support its claims is based on three main pillars that directly affect the daily lives of workers. The first critical point is the maintenance of purchasing power. Despite inflation, the association highlights how the constant increase in health insurance premiums represents a burden not included in the official cost-of-living index, significantly eroding the disposable income of families. Forecasts for 2026 suggest inflation slightly higher than the previous year, with uncertainties linked to the geopolitical situation and the cost of oil that could further influence consumer prices. For those wishing to delve into the impact of fixed costs on the family budget, the [cost of living in Switzerland](nav:cost-of-living) remains an essential parameter to monitor.
### The recovery of salary arrears The second point concerns the lack of salary adjustments accumulated during the years 2022 and 2023. During this period, characterized by high inflation, most banks did not provide full compensation for the rise in the cost of living. ASIB points out that, in many cases, employees have not seen pay raises for years, and even in the most recent two-year periods, adjustments have been rare and partial. This delay must, according to the association, be bridged to realign wages with the actual cost of living. Productivity represents the third pillar: the introduction of new digital technologies and artificial intelligence has allowed banks to optimize processes. At the same time, staff reductions in numerous institutions have increased the workload for those who remained. ASIB argues that if fewer employees provide the same or higher performance, productivity gains should be fairly redistributed. Workers, therefore, are not only asking for an adjustment to prices, but for recognition of the added value created through the operational efficiency and technological innovation that characterize the Swiss financial sector today.

The transparency requested by the ASIB should be viewed as a protective tool: every employee has the right to request clarification on performance evaluation criteria and the parameters that determine salary increases. item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The **B permit** is a renewable long‑term residence permit - LAMal insurance must be taken out within 3 months of arrival - AVS/AHV contributions amount to 5.3% for the employee
## Key facts - What: B residence permit - When: not yet specified - Where: Canton Jura - Who: Cantonal migration office (competent authority) - Amount: not yet specified - AVS/AHV contribution: 5.3% employee (10.6% total) - LAMal: mandatory within 3 months, premiums vary by canton - Taxation: 3 levels – federal, cantonal, communal
The B residence permit is governed by the Federal Act on Foreign Nationals and Borders (SECO). It is a long‑term residence permit, renewable upon expiry, which allows the holder to settle permanently in Switzerland. In the Canton of Jura, the authority for issuing and renewing it lies with the Cantonal Migration Office, the body responsible for verifying compliance with the legal requirements.
### How the B permit works The B permit is distinct from the L permit (short‑term, up to one year) and the C permit (settlement, usually after ten years of residence). To obtain or renew the B, the regulations require proof of regular accommodation, LAMal insurance coverage within three months of arrival, and regular AVS/AHV contributions. LAMal insurance is mandatory for all residents, with deductibles ranging from CHF 300 to CHF 2500 depending on income.
The Swiss tax system provides three levels of taxation: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and communal tax, each with its own multipliers. This affects the tax burden of the B permit holder, who must file tax returns at the federal and cantonal levels, taking into account the deductions provided for AVS/AHV contributions and LAMal insurance expenses. Managing these aspects is crucial for those who intend to stay long‑term in the canton.
Respecting renewal deadlines is essential: the holder must submit the application within the time limits set by the cantonal office, attaching the required documents (residence certificate, LAMal insurance certificate, AVS/AHV contribution extracts). Failure to do so can result in loss of the residence permit. ## Practical analysis The B permit directly affects different areas of daily life in Switzerland. From a tax point of view, the holder is subject to direct federal tax, VAT (which affects goods and services) and cantonal and municipal taxes, with multipliers varying from canton to canton. In the case of the Jura, the cantonal legislation establishes a specific multiplier that applies to the cantonal tax, while the municipalities apply an additional multiplier on the result.
### Implications for Social Security and Health AVS/AHV contributions, equal to 5.3% of the employee's salary, are mandatory for all B permit holders. These contributions finance old-age pension (AVS) and disability insurance (AI). In parallel, LAMal insurance must be taken out within three months; the premium is determined by the canton of residence and income, and deductibles can range from CHF 300 to CHF 2500. Compliance with these obligations guarantees access to health care and a future pension.
### Comparison with other permits Compared to the L permit, the B offers greater stability because it is renewable and not limited to one year. However, unlike the C permit, the B does not automatically confer the right to vote or the possibility of naturalization; for the latter it is necessary to have lived at least ten years (eight for EU/EFTA citizens) and meet cantonal and municipal requirements.

Verify the deadlines – the expiry date of the B permit is indicated on the residence document; the renewal application must be submitted at least 30 days before the expiry at the Cantonal Migration Office. 3. Fill out the renewal form – the form is available on the official website of the canton of Jura; you must provide personal data, employment situation and confirm compliance with AVS/AHV contributions and LAMal. 4. item.description: Find out how the B permit works in the Canton of Jura, from the documentation to the renewal procedure, with a focus on taxation and compulsory insurance.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - Permesso B: durata e rinnovo gestiti dall'ufficio cantonale della migrazione - Imposta federale, cantonale e comunale: tre livelli di tassazione - LAMal obbligatoria entro 3 mesi dall'arrivo - Contributi AVS/AI e LPP applicabili a tutti i titolari di permesso B
## Fatti chiave - **Cosa**: Permesso di dimora B rinnovabile nel Cantone di Giura - Quando: non ancora specificato - Dove: Cantone di Giura, ufficio cantonale della migrazione competente - Chi: autorità cantonale responsabile dei permessi di soggiorno - Importo: non ancora specificato
Il permesso di dimora B è il principale strumento di soggiorno a lungo termine per cittadini non svizzeri che intendono vivere e lavorare in Svizzera. Nel Cantone di Giura, la competenza spetta all'ufficio cantonale della migrazione, che gestisce sia la concessione iniziale sia il rinnovo. La normativa prevede che il permesso B sia rinnovabile, ma la fonte non specifica la durata esatta né i criteri di valutazione. 📊
Dal punto di vista fiscale, i titolari di permesso B sono soggetti a tre livelli di imposta: imposta federale diretta (IFD), imposta cantonale e imposta comunale. Ogni cantone applica una legge propria e un moltiplicatore specifico, mentre i comuni aggiungono un ulteriore moltiplicatore sul cantonale.
Sul versante della sicurezza sociale, tutti i residenti, inclusi i titolari di permesso B, contribuiscono all’AVS/AHV, all’assicurazione invalidità (AI) e all’assicurazione contro la perdita di guadagno (IPG) con una quota dipendente del 5,3 %. Il datore di lavoro completa il 10,6 % totale. Inoltre, le assicurazioni pensionistiche obbligatorie (LPP/BVG) prevedono aliquote progressive in base all’età, con un minimo del 7 % per chi ha 25‑34 anni e fino al 18 % per chi supera i 55 anni.
L’assicurazione malattia obbligatoria (LAMal/KVG) deve essere stipulata entro tre mesi dall’arrivo. I premi variano per cantone e per situazione familiare, con franchigie che vanno da 300 a 2500 CHF. Il Cantone di Giura, come tutti gli altri, offre un sussidio per ridurre il premio in base al reddito.
Il permesso B non è confondibile con altri permessi: il permesso L è a breve durata (fino a un anno), il permesso C è il domicilio permanente (di norma 10 anni di residenza, 5 per UE/AELS) e il permesso G è riservato ai frontalieri. La distinzione è importante perché influisce su diritti di lavoro, accesso a servizi sociali e obblighi fiscali. ### Implicazioni fiscali e previdenziali per i titolari di permesso B in Giura
Chi ottiene il permesso B nel Cantone di Giura entra immediatamente nel sistema fiscale a tre livelli. L’imposta federale diretta è uniforme a livello nazionale, mentre l’imposta cantonale varia in base al cantone di residenza; nel caso di Giura, il cantone applica il proprio coefficiente di moltiplicazione, che può differire da quello di Zurigo o di Berna. I comuni aggiungono un ulteriore moltiplicatore, rendendo la pressione fiscale locale una combinazione di tre parametri distinti. Per un residente con reddito medio, la differenza tra il carico fiscale di Giura e quello di un cantone con aliquota più alta può tradursi in una variazione di diverse centinaia di franchi all’anno.
Dal punto di vista della previdenza, tutti i titolari di permesso B sono obbligati a versare i contributi AVS/AHV e AI. Questi contributi sono calcolati sul salario lordo e, insieme all’assicurazione contro la perdita di guadagno (IPG), costituiscono la base per la futura pensione di vecchiaia. La LPP/BVG, invece, è collegata al salario coordinato: le aliquote crescono con l’età, garantendo un accumulo più consistente per i lavoratori più anziani.
L’obbligo di stipulare la LAMal entro tre mesi dall’arrivo ha un impatto diretto sul bilancio familiare. I premi variano per cantone; nel caso di Giura, il premio medio è allineato a quello nazionale, ma il sussidio cantonale può ridurre l’importo in base al reddito.
Un altro aspetto rilevante è la possibilità di accedere al mercato del lavoro. Il permesso B consente di lavorare in qualsiasi settore, senza le restrizioni del permesso L. Tuttavia, l’assenza di un salario minimo federale significa che il livello retributivo dipende dal contratto collettivo cantonale o dall’accordo individuale. In Giura, alcuni settori hanno introdotto un salario minimo cantonale, ma non tutti; quindi, il titolare di permesso B deve verificare le condizioni specifiche del proprio contratto.
### Confronto con altri cantoni
Se confrontiamo Giura con un cantone come Zurigo, la differenza più evidente riguarda l’imposizione fiscale: Zurigo ha una delle aliquote cantonali più alte, mentre Giura è tradizionalmente più favorevole per i contribuenti con redditi medio‑bassi. Sul fronte della LAMal, i premi sono simili, ma il sussidio giurano‑cinese può essere più generoso rispetto a cantoni più ricchi. Per quanto riguarda la LPP, le aliquote sono uniformi a livello nazionale, quindi non ci sono differenze sostanziali.
Queste considerazioni mostrano come il permesso B, pur essendo un documento di soggiorno, influisca direttamente su aspetti economici quotidiani: tassazione, contributi previdenziali, assicurazione sanitaria e condizioni di lavoro.
### Scenari ipotetici
Un titolare di permesso B che si trasferisce da un cantone ad alta imposizione a Giura potrebbe vedere una riduzione del carico fiscale netto del 5‑10 %. Al contrario, chi si sposta da Giura a un cantone con salario minimo più alto potrebbe beneficiare di stipendi più elevati, ma anche di una maggiore pressione fiscale. Questi scenari, sebbene generici, evidenziano l’importanza di valutare il contesto cantonale prima di prendere decisioni di residenza.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### How to request or renew a residence permit B in Giura
1. **Check the basic requirements** – The source indicates that the requirements, documents to be produced, and duration have not yet been specified. In general, it is necessary to demonstrate one's identity, the availability of accommodation in Giura, a work contract or sufficient resources for subsistence, and LAMal insurance coverage within three months of arrival.
2. Gather documentation – Prepare the following documents, typically required for a permit B (although the source does not list specific details): - Valid passport - Birth certificate translated and legalized - Work contract or proof of income - LAMal insurance attestation - Proof of residence (rental agreement or landlord's declaration)
3. Submit the application – The application must be sent to the competent cantonal migration office in Giura. This can be done in person or, where provided, via the canton’s online portal.
4. Payment of fees – The source does not specify the amounts, so it is advisable to consult the official website of the migration office to know the presentation fees and any administrative costs.
5. Timing – After submission, the office examines the application. The duration of the procedure is not indicated in the source; generally, the process can take from 4 to 8 weeks. It is prudent to request written confirmation of response times.
6. Renewal – The permit B is renewable. Before expiry, a new application must be submitted with updated documentation (current work contract, valid LAMal insurance, new proof of residence). The renewal follows the same procedure described above.
Strumenti utili – To calculate the fiscal impact of permit B in Giura, use our [salary calculator](nav:calculator). You can also compare the cost of living in Giura with other cantons via our [cost of living](nav:cost-of-living). If you have doubts about LAMal coverage, visit the [LAMal](nav:health) section.
### Quick checklist for renewal - Check the expiry date of the current permit - Update the work contract or proof of income - Verify the validity of LAMal insurance - Gather a new proof of residence - Complete the renewal form available on the migration office's website - Pay any renewal fees - Send the application within 30 days of expiry to avoid interruptions of stay
By following these steps, B permit holders can autonomously manage the entire process, minimizing administrative delays and maintaining fiscal and insurance regularity.

item.title: Health insurance premiums in the canton of Jura: reductions and bands 2024
item.description: Practical Guide to LAMal Awards in the Canton of Jura: Deductible Bands, Alternative Models, and Requirements to Achieve Cantonal Premium Reduction.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Compulsory health insurance (LAMal) involves per capita premiums that vary by canton. - In the Canton of Jura, there are 6 adult deductible tiers (CHF 300–2500). - Alternative models (HMO, Telmed) can reduce premiums by up to 20%. - Cantonal premium reduction depends on income and assets.
## Key Facts - **What**: LAMal premiums and reductions in the Canton of Jura. - Legal basis: Federal Health Insurance Act (LAMal). - Adult deductibles: CHF 300/500/1000/1500/2000/2500. - Premium reduction: Cantonal subsidy based on income/assets. - Alternative models: HMO, Telmed, healthcare networks.
In the Canton of Jura, as throughout Switzerland, basic health insurance (LAMal/KVG) is mandatory for all residents. Premiums, set annually by health insurers, vary significantly between cantons and insurance models. The Jura-sano.ch system, the cantonal portal, provides official information on available premiums and reductions.
### Deductible Tiers and Premiums Adult insured individuals can choose from six annual deductible tiers: CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, or 2500. The choice directly influences the premium amount: higher deductibles reduce the monthly premium but increase out-of-pocket costs in case of treatment. For example, a deductible of CHF 2500 can reduce the premium by up to 30% compared to the minimum tier (CHF 300).
### Alternative Models Alternative insurance models offer reduced premiums in exchange for restrictions on access to care. The main ones are: - HMO: Coordinated care through a family doctor or a medical center. - Telmed: Preliminary telephone consultation with service doctors. - Healthcare network: A predetermined list of care providers.
These models can lower premiums by up to 20% compared to the standard model but limit the free choice of doctor.
### Cantonal Premium Reduction The Canton of Jura grants subsidies to reduce LAMal premiums for families and individuals with limited income and assets. The main requirements are: 1. Legal residence in the Canton of Jura. 2. Taxable income below the cantonal threshold (2024 figures not yet specified). 3. Net worth below the defined limit (excluding primary residence).
Applications must be submitted annually to the Cantonal Office of Public Health by March 31st, attaching the tax return and asset documents. ## Practical implications for policyholders The choice of deductible and insurance model requires a careful analysis of your health risk profile and financial capacity.
### Savings Scenarios Case 1: A single person without chronic diseases could opt for a CHF 2500 deductible and Telmed model, reducing the monthly premium by about CHF 150 compared to the standard model with minimum deductible. However, in the event of an unforeseen hospitalisation, it would pay up to CHF 2500 before repayment.
Case 2: A family with young children might prefer the CHF 300 deductible and HMO model for immediate access to affiliated paediatricians, accepting a higher premium but predictable costs.
### Comparison with other cantons While Swiss average LAMal premiums increase (UST/BFS), the Canton of Jura maintains relatively low premiums thanks to cantonal cost containment policies. However, cantonal reductions are less generous than cantons with greater fiscal capacity, such as Zurich or Vaud.
## # Reduction Procedures The Public Health Office jura-sano.ch verifies income and assets through: 1. **Tax Return **: Gross Income and Deductions 2. Extract from the Land Registry: Real Estate Properties 3. Bank statements: Accounts and investments
Subsidies are calculated automatically and reported by June. The beneficiaries receive a certificate to be presented to the sickness fund for the adjustment of the premium.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). ## How to get the premium reduction in the Jura ### Operating steps 1. ** Eligibility Check **: Check the 2024 income/equity limits on jura-sano.ch (available from January) 2. Collect documents: Tax return, bank statements, land register 3. Apply: Online or by post to the Cantonal Health Office by 31 March 4. Wait for decision: The approved subsidies are valid from 1 January of the current year
### Useful tools - Premium calculator: Simulate deductible/model premiums on comparis.ch or jura-sano.ch - Family check-up: Evaluate the annual health risk to choose the optimal deductible - Cantonal consultancy: Free jura-sano.ch service to optimise coverage
Critical ⚠️ deadlines: Applications submitted after 31 March do not receive retroactive reductions. New residents have 3 months from arrival to take out basic insurance.
[Verifica idoneità alla riduzione premi](nav:health)
### Recent Changes From 2025, the Canton of Jura introduces a system of automatic reductions for recipients of complementary AVS/AI benefits, simplifying procedures. It is advisable to monitor updates on jura-sano.ch for changes to income thresholds.
Practical 💡 tip: Combine high deductible + alternative model + cantonal subsidy to maximize savings, if the risk profile allows it.

item.title: Lonza invests in the USA: new pharmaceutical plant in Oregon
item.description: Swiss pharmaceutical giant Lonza will build a new manufacturing facility in Bend, Oregon, with completion expected by 2029.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Lonza will build a new facility in Bend, Oregon - Completion of the structure is expected by 2029 - Initial creation of over 80 new jobs - Investment defined as significant by the pharmaceutical group
## Key facts - **What**: Construction of a new commercial manufacturing plant - When: Completion expected by 2029 - Where: Bend, Oregon, United States - Who: Lonza - Amount: Amount not yet specified
The Swiss pharmaceutical industry is further strengthening its presence and investments in the United States. The Lonza group has officially announced the construction of a new facility in Bend, in the state of Oregon. The facility will be dedicated to the commercial production of spray-dried active ingredient dispersions. According to what was communicated by the Swiss pharmaceutical company, the completion of the work is expected during the year 2029. The financial operation has been defined by company management as a significant investment, although the exact monetary amount was not disclosed in the official press release issued by the company.
### Pharmaceutical technology details
The industrial project focuses on advanced technology capable of significantly improving the solubility and, consequently, the bioavailability of active ingredients that are poorly soluble. From the perspective of the global pharmaceutical market, demand for these particular manufacturing processes is experiencing steady growth, driven by the increasing complexity in the development of modern medicines. The new facility in Oregon will allow Lonza to respond promptly to this growing demand, consolidating its technological positioning in the advanced pharmaceutical manufacturing sector on an international scale. ### Employment impact and supply chains
The launch of this major industrial project in the United States will initially lead to the creation of over eighty new highly skilled jobs in the Bend region. The strategic decision to expand production capacity overseas responds to precise logics of operational proximity to important customers and strengthening the resilience of regional supply chains. Bringing production closer to the main outlet markets allows the company to reduce the risks related to international logistics and optimise delivery times for the local pharmaceutical industry.
### Corporate Strategy and Leadership
Managing Director Wolfgang Wienand underlined the strategic importance of the transaction for the future of the Swiss group. The investment in the Bend headquarters reflects the firm belief that the United States will remain a leading source of pharmaceutical innovation and a key market for Lonza. This move fits perfectly into the company strategy called One Lonza, which aims to concentrate investments where it is possible to generate maximum economic value for customers and, ultimately, for patients. The German manager, fifty-four years old and with a past as a leading fencer, has been leading the Rhenish company since July 2024.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### Profile and history of the Lonza group
Founded in 1897, Lonza has a long industrial history rooted in Switzerland. The company was originally born in Gampel, in the Valais Canton, on the banks of the river Lonza, which represents a tributary of the Rhone. During the twentieth century, precisely in 1909, the headquarters were moved to Visp, also in the Valais Canton. Subsequently, in 1974, the company became part of Alusuisse's orbit, and then left it in 1999 and obtained an official listing on the stock exchange. In 2002 the group's main operational centre was moved to Basel.
### Position in the Swiss financial markets
Today Lonza is one of the most important industrial companies in the Confederation, with a global workforce of twenty thousand employees. During the 2025 financial year, the company recorded a total turnover of 6.5 billion Swiss francs. Thanks to these economic data and its solidity, the company is part of the SMI, the stock index that groups the twenty main securities of the Swiss financial market. To learn more about the management of corporate finances, taxation and investments in Switzerland, see [calcolatore stipendio e imposte](nav:calculator).

item.title: Cantonal taxes Jura: rates, brackets and deductions 2024
item.description: Practical guide to the tax system of the Canton of Jura: three-level structure, municipal multipliers, allowable deductions and official portal for the declaration.
item.content:encoded:
## In breve - Il Cantone Giura applica imposte su tre livelli: federale, cantonale e comunale - Le aliquote cantonali sono progressive; i comuni applicano un moltiplicatore sull'imposta cantonale - Le deduzioni seguono principi federali con integrazioni cantonali specifiche - La dichiarazione si presenta online tramite il portale dell'amministrazione fiscale giurassiana
## Fatti chiave - **Cosa**: Imposte cantonali e comunali nel Cantone Giura - Quando: Scadenza dichiarazione ordinaria 31 marzo (proroghe possibili) - Dove: Cantone Giura, Svizzera - Chi: Amministrazione fiscale cantonale del Giura (Service des contributions) - Importo: Aliquote progressive per scaglioni di reddito e sostanza; moltiplicatori comunali variabili
Il sistema fiscale svizzero si articola su tre livelli: l'imposta federale diretta (IFD) gestita dall'AFC/ESTV, l'imposta cantonale e l'imposta comunale, entrambe di competenza delle amministrazioni cantonali. Nel Cantone Giura, come in tutti i cantoni, la legge fiscale cantonale definisce gli scaglioni di reddito e di sostanza, le aliquote base e le deduzioni ammesse. I comuni giurassiani applicano poi un moltiplicatore (coefficiente) sull'imposta cantonale netta per determinare l'imposta comunale dovuta.
### Struttura a tre livelli e competenze L'IFD è identica per tutti i contribuenti svizzeri e viene calcolata sull'imponibile federale. L'imposta cantonale del Giura segue una tariffa progressiva per scaglioni: all'aumentare del reddito imponibile (o della sostanza imponibile) si applicano aliquote marginali crescenti. L'imposta comunale non ha tariffa propria: è il risultato dell'imposta cantonale moltiplicata per il coefficiente comunale, che ogni comune fissa annualmente. Questa architettura rende il carico fiscale finale diverso da comune a comune pur restando all'interno dello stesso cantone.
La distinzione di competenze è rigida: AFC/ESTV gestisce IFD e IVA; le amministrazioni cantonali (nel Giura il Service des contributions) gestiscono imposte cantonali e comunali; UFAS/BSV si occupa di previdenza sociale (AVS/AI/LPP) e non fissa imposte; UST/BFS produce statistiche e non fissa aliquote. ### Aliquote, scaglioni e moltiplicatori comunali Le aliquote cantonali del Giura sono pubblicate ogni anno nel tariffario ufficiale e si applicano per scaglioni di reddito netto imponibile (dopo deduzioni) e di sostanza netta imponibile. Non esiste un'aliquota unica: il sistema è progressivo a scaglioni, quindi la prima tranche di reddito è tassata all'aliquota più bassa, la tranche successiva all'aliquota superiore, e così via. L'imposta cantonale lorda che ne risulta viene poi ridotta degli eventuali abbuoni o crediti d'imposta cantonali per arrivare all'imposta cantonale netta.
Su questa base netta si applica il moltiplicatore comunale. Ogni comune del Giura delibera annualmente il proprio coefficiente (es. 1,45; 1,60; 1,30 ecc.). L'imposta comunale = imposta cantonale netta × moltiplicatore comunale. La somma di imposta cantonale netta + imposta comunale costituisce l'imposta cantonale/comunale complessiva. A questa si aggiunge l'IFD per ottenere l'imposta totale dovuta.
### Deduzioni ammesse: principi federali e specificità cantonali Le deduzioni seguono in larga misura i principi del diritto federale armonizzato (LIFD), ma il Cantone Giura può prevedere deduzioni supplementari o parametri propri (es. deduzioni per figli, per spese di guadagno, per premi LAMal/KVG, per versamenti nel pilastro 3a, per interessi passivi, per spese mediche eccedenti una franchigia). L'elenco preciso e gli importi massimi deducibili per l'anno d'imposta in corso sono indicati nelle istruzioni ufficiali della dichiarazione d'imposta giurassiana e sul portale dell'amministrazione fiscale.
Un aspetto pratico rilevante: i contributi sociali trattenuti alla fonte (AVS/AI/IPG 5,3% a carico dipendente, AD/AC 1,1%, LAINF/LAA secondo settore, LPP sul salario coordinato con aliquote per fasce d'età) riducono il reddito lordo per determinare il reddito netto imponibile. I premi LAMal/KVG non sono contributi salariali né tasse, ma sono deducibili entro i limiti cantonali.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Deadlines, procedure and online portal The ordinary tax return must be submitted by 31 March of the year following the tax year (unless extensions are granted upon request to the tax administration). The Canton of Jura provides the official portal for electronic declaration (e-tax/online declaration), which guides the taxpayer step by step: import of pre-filled data (salary certificates, bank certificates, etc.), manual entry of missing items, automatic calculation of the taxable amount and estimated tax, sending digitally signed.
Those who do not receive the pre-filled declaration or prefer paper can request the forms from the tax administration. After submission, the office issues the final taxation with the taxation decision (Veranlagungsverfügung/ décision de taxation). You can lodge a complaint with the competent appeal authority within 30 days.
## # Taxpayer-friendly tools To simulate the impact of income, deductions, municipality of residence and family situation, the site's salary/tax calculator allows you to compare scenarios. Those who have to coordinate IFD, cantonal/municipal and social security (AVS/LPP/pillar 3a) find an overview in the payroll calculator. For the actual declaration, the direct link to the Jura e-tax portal is the fastest channel.

item.title: Stefan Leist appointed Deputy Director Federal Administration of Finance
item.description: Karin Keller-Sutter appoints Stefan Leist as AFF Deputy Director from 1 October 2026. Already leading the Financial Policy Division since 1 March 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Federal Councilor Karin Keller‑Sutter appoints Stefan Leist as deputy director of the Federal Finance Administration (AFF) from 1 October 2026 - The Federal Council was informed in the meeting of 9 September 2026 - Leist has been leading the Financial Policy and Equalisation division since 1 March 2026
## Key facts - **What**: Appointment as deputy director of the Federal Finance Administration - When: Takes office 1 October 2026, decision 9 September 2026 - Where: Federal Finance Administration, Bern - Who: Stefan Leist, 45, PhD in political economy - Importance: Key role for financial policy and inter‑cantonal equalisation
Federal Councilor Karin Keller‑Sutter, head of the Federal Department of Finance, appointed Stefan Leist as deputy director of the Federal Finance Administration (AFF) effective 1 October 2026. The decision was communicated to the Federal Council in the meeting of 9 September 2026.
### Professional background and skills Stefan Leist, 45, has many years of experience within the Federal Administration. Since 1 March 2026 he has already held the position of deputy director of the AFF and head of the Financial Policy, Financial Equalisation and Financial Statistics division. He earned a degree in political economy at the University of Bern and obtained his PhD in 2012, the year he joined the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO). Before moving to the AFF, he headed the Labour Market Analysis and Social Policy unit at SECO and was deputy head of the Economic Policy Directorate.
### The role of the AFF in the federal system The Federal Finance Administration is the central unit for managing the Confederation's finances. Its main tasks include preparing the federal budget, managing public debt, financial policy and financial equalisation between the Confederation and the cantons. The division led by Leist deals precisely with these strategic dossiers, including financial statistics that feed national fiscal policy decisions. ### Implications for Swiss financial policy The appointment of Leist comes at a time when federal financial policy must confront structural challenges: the brake on indebtedness, the equalisation of resources among cantons and the evolution of the federal direct tax. The Financial Policy, Financial Equalisation and Financial Statistics division that he leads is the analytical engine behind the proposals that the Federal Council submits to Parliament for the budget and the final accounts.
### Continuity and signals from within The fact that Leist was already deputy director of the AFF since 1 March 2026 signals operational continuity: the promotion to deputy director formalises a role that he has de facto exercised for six months. His career at SECO, where he acquired expertise on the labour market and economic policy, brings to the AFF a transversal vision that links federal revenues, social spending and employment dynamics. This hybrid profile is rare at the top of the financial administration and could strengthen coordination between the Federal Department of Finance and the Federal Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research.
### Financial equalisation: the hot dossier Among the most sensitive dossiers that Leist's division handles is the financial equalisation 2028‑2035, currently in preparation. The mechanism redistributes resources between the Confederation and the cantons and between wealthy cantons and cantons with lower fiscal capacity. Any adjustment of the parameters — fiscal power, burden indices, compensation for cases of rigidity — has direct effects on cantonal budgets and, by reflection, on cantonal and municipal taxes that citizens and businesses pay. The continuity guaranteed by Leist, who knows the UST/BFS statistical models underlying the calculations, reduces the risk of technical discontinuity in the next cycle.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ### What changes for those who live and work in Switzerland The appointment does not directly change rates or deadlines for taxpayers. However, stability at the top of the AFF is a necessary condition for the budget, final account and equalization processes to respect constitutional deadlines. Delays or uncertainties in these processes have an impact on cantonal estimates and, ultimately, on the taxes that residents — including border workers — pay at the cantonal and municipal levels.
### How to follow the work of the AFF Financial policy documents, equalisation reports and financial statistics are published on the AFF and UST/BFS website. Those who want to monitor the impact of federal decisions on their canton can consult the cantonal estimates, usually adopted between November and December for the following year. To estimate the impact of direct federal tax and cantonal/municipal taxes on your income, it is useful to compare the updated municipal multipliers.

item.title: F-35: Amherd Risks Liability for Extra Costs
item.description: CdG ascertains that Amherd knew of the F-35 cost risks months earlier. Three-year prescription expiring, Wyssmann asks for an interruption.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The CdG established that Amherd was aware of the risks of extra costs on the F-35s months before informing the Federal Council. - No final price was ever set for the purchase of the 36 jets. - UDC National Councillor Wyssmann is asking to block the statute of limitations for potential liability actions. - The three-year deadline to take legal action may expire soon.
## Key facts - **What**: Investigation by the National Council's Committee of Administration regarding the purchase of the F-35s. - When: Report recently published; three-year statute of limitations is running. - Where: Bern, federal level. - Who: Former Federal Councillor Viola Amherd, CdG, National Councillor Rémy Wyssmann (UDC), Federal Council. - Amount: Potential damage not yet specified; previous Bischof case involved 112,500 francs. - Legal basis: Art. 5 para. 3 of the Ordinance on the Liability Act.
### The CdG investigation and its findings The National Council's Committee of Administration (CdG) has concluded its investigations into the methods used to purchase the 36 F-35 jets. According to the report, former Federal Councillor Viola Amherd was aware, months before informing the Federal Council, of the risk of additional costs. Furthermore, a final price for the contract was never set. Amherd, currently in Oslo for the funeral of Norwegian King Harald V, has so far chosen silence and has not responded to journalists' requests.
### The debate on legal liability In Bern, the issue of personal liability is at the center of political debate. UDC National Councillor Rémy Wyssmann had asked a year ago for the Federal Council to adopt 'all necessary measures' so that potential civil liability claims against Amherd and the officials involved would not fall under the statute of limitations. At the time, the Federal Council had recommended rejecting the request, arguing that there were 'no sufficient concrete indications either of the presence of damage, or of unlawful conduct.' However, it had assured that the competent authorities would evaluate legal actions should such indications emerge.
### Jurisdiction and precedents According to Article 5, paragraph 3, of the Ordinance on the Liability Act, jurisdiction for potential legal actions against Amherd lies with the Federal Council as a whole; for the officials involved, liability falls under the Department of Defense. A historical precedent is represented by the case of Councillor of States Pirmin Bischof (Centre), who in the 1990s was held personally responsible for the failure of the Solothurn Cantonal Bank and paid 112,500 francs. Former Socialist National Councillor Pierre-Alain Fridez considers the investigation insufficient and calls for the establishment of a parliamentary committee of inquiry, extending the in-depth analysis to the choice of the F-35 model.

item.title: Wages and work Thurgau: sectors, levels and contracts
item.description: In the canton of Thurgau there is no federal minimum wage; the weekly hours are 45 or 50 depending on the sector, with AVS/AHV contributions at 5.3% for the employee.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - No federal minimum wage, any canton-specific not yet specified - Maximum weekly schedule of 45 or 50 hours depending on the sector - Employee AVS/AHV contributions 5.3% (10.6% total with employer) - LAMal required for all residents - Direct federal tax, VAT and three tax levels (federal, cantonal, municipal)
## Key facts - What: Contributory scheme AVS/AHV, LPP and LAMal - When: Current, in force for years without recent changes - Where: Canton of Thurgau, valid at national level - Who: Employees, employers, cantonal authorities - Amount: Employee AVS/AHV contribution 5.3% - **What**: Maximum working hours 45 h (industry, offices, sales) or 50 h (other sectors) - When: Minimum holiday 4 weeks (5 under 20) - Who: SECO, UST/BFS, BNS/SNB provide statistical data
The canton of Thurgau, like all Swiss cantons, is located in the federal framework in which there is no minimum wage at the national level; the presence of a cantonal minimum, if provided, is not indicated in the source and therefore remains "not yet specified". Working time regulations set a limit of 45 hours per week for industrial, office and sales sectors, while other sectors can reach 50 hours. Holidays are guaranteed for a minimum of four weeks, with an extension to five weeks for workers under twenty.
### Regulatory frameworks and mandatory contributions Employees are subject to a 📊 The labour market in Thurgau is characterised by a strong presence of collective agreements, although the source does not list specific agreements. In the absence of a cantonal minimum wage, wages are negotiated between unions and employers, often based on the level of training. The sectors that traditionally employ the most include the mechanical industry, financial services and alpine tourism; these sectors require skills ranging from professional qualifications to specialist degrees.
Without a cantonal minimum, the wage difference between training levels can be more marked than in cantons with a fixed threshold. A worker with vocational training (CAP) could earn a basic salary which, once the AVS/AHV, LPP and LAMal contributions are applied, translates into a net lower than a graduate with the same working hours. However, collective agreements often provide for wage brackets by grade of qualification, reducing the gap.

## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the [pension planner](nav:pension) and the [pillar 3 simulator](nav:pillar3). 💡 For those living or planning to work in the canton of Thurgau, the operational process begins with verifying the collective labor agreements applicable to your sector. Here are the recommended steps:
1. **Identify the employment sector** – consult the cantonal website or SECO publications to understand which collective agreements are in effect. 2. Retrieve the agreement text – often available on the industry union's portal or the cantonal labor authority's website. 3. Calculate net pay – use the [salary calculator](nav:calculator) by entering gross salary, weekly hours (45 or 50), and mandatory contributions (AVS/AHV 5.3%, AD/AC 1.1%, LAA/LAI 0.7–1.5%). 4. Verify health insurance coverage – within three months of relocation, it is mandatory to take out health insurance; choose the most suitable deductible (300–2500 CHF) and check for any cantonal reductions. 5. Declare taxes – complete the federal direct tax return and the cantonal/municipal return, taking into account the municipal multiplier. For the final calculation, you can use the tax calculator. 6. Monitor updates – changes to collective agreements or salary thresholds are published by UST/BFS and SECO; subscribing to cantonal newsletters is useful for not missing deadlines.
If you hold a residence permit (B, C, or G), you must also verify the validity of the permit with the SEM and, if necessary, renew it before the expiration date.
